w17160.full:
Both Messiahs To Resemble Urwa Bin Masud?

The allegation of the non Ahmadi Muslims is that in Sahih Muslim the Holy Prophetsaw has been recorded to have said that Isaas who was sent to Bani Israel resembled Urwa bin Masud, while in Sahih Muslim again in regards to the latter day messiah, hesaw has also said the same. First of all when we look at the most authentic book after the Qur’an, Bukhari, we are told that the messiahs would not resemble each other and be two different people.

Hesaw states in regards to the description of the messiahas sent to Bani Israel:

حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا إِسْرَائِيلُ، أَخْبَرَنَا عُثْمَانُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ “‏ رَأَيْتُ عِيسَى وَمُوسَى وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ، فَأَمَّا عِيسَى فَأَحْمَرُ جَعْدٌ عَرِيضُ الصَّدْرِ، وَأَمَّا مُوسَى فَآدَمُ جَسِيمٌ سَبْطٌ كَأَنَّهُ مِنْ رِجَالِ الزُّطِّ ‏”‏‏.‏

Narrated Ibn `Abbas: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, “I saw Moses, Jesus and Abraham (on the night of my Ascension to the heavens). Jesus was of red complexion, curly hair and a broad chest. Moses was of brown complexion, straight hair and tall stature as if he was from the people of Az-Zutt.” (Bukhari Volume 5, book 55, Hadith 648)

Hesaw states in regards to the Messiah of the end times who was to be from our ummah:

حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ الْمُنْذِرِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو ضَمْرَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ذَكَرَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمًا بَيْنَ ظَهْرَىِ النَّاسِ الْمَسِيحَ الدَّجَّالَ، فَقَالَ ‏”‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِأَعْوَرَ، أَلاَ إِنَّ الْمَسِيحَ الدَّجَّالَ أَعْوَرُ الْعَيْنِ الْيُمْنَى، كَأَنَّ عَيْنَهُ عِنَبَةٌ طَافِيَةٌ ‏”‏‏.‏ ‏”‏ وَأَرَانِي اللَّيْلَةَ عِنْدَ الْكَعْبَةِ فِي الْمَنَامِ، فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ آدَمُ كَأَحْسَنِ مَا يُرَى مِنْ أُدْمِ الرِّجَالِ، تَضْرِبُ لِمَّتُهُ بَيْنَ مَنْكِبَيْهِ، رَجِلُ الشَّعَرِ، يَقْطُرُ رَأْسُهُ مَاءً، وَاضِعًا يَدَيْهِ عَلَى مَنْكِبَىْ رَجُلَيْنِ وَهْوَ يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَنْ هَذَا فَقَالُوا هَذَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ‏.‏ ثُمَّ رَأَيْتُ رَجُلاً وَرَاءَهُ جَعْدًا قَطَطًا أَعْوَرَ عَيْنِ الْيُمْنَى كَأَشْبَهِ مَنْ رَأَيْتُ بِابْنِ قَطَنٍ، وَاضِعًا يَدَيْهِ عَلَى مَنْكِبَىْ رَجُلٍ، يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ، فَقُلْتُ مَنْ هَذَا قَالُوا الْمَسِيحُ الدَّجَّالُ ‏”‏‏.‏ تَابَعَهُ عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ عَنْ نَافِعٍ‏.‏

Narrated `Abdullah: The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the Masih Ad-Dajjal in front of the people saying, Allah is not one-eyed while Masih Ad-Dajjal is blind in the right eye and his eye looks like a bulging out grape. While sleeping near the Ka`ba last night, I saw in my dream a man of brown color the best one can see amongst brown color and his hair was long that it fell between his shoulders. His hair was lank and water was dribbling from his head and he was placing his hands on the shoulders of two men while circumambulating the Ka`ba. I asked, ‘Who is this?’ They replied, ‘This is Jesus, son of Mary.’ Behind him I saw a man who had very curly hair and was blind in the right eye, resembling Ibn Qatan (i.e. an infidel) in appearance. He was placing his hands on the shoulders of a person while performing Tawaf around the Ka`ba. I asked, ‘Who is this? ‘They replied, ‘The Masih, Ad-Dajjal.’ (sahih Bukhari Volume 4, book 55, Hadith #649)

There have been attempts to state that the Prophetsaw did not mention Isaasbeing of reddish complexion. This is a total confusion which is not true at all. All the descriptions of the Messiah sent to Bani Israel always mentions reddish complexion, while the latter always mentions brown complexion. The Prophet Muhammadsaw has clearly showed a distinction between the Messiahs.

Another beautiful point to notice is that all Muslims know that the one to revive Islam would be the same Messiah who was prophesied about. We all know that Isaas was of Bani Israel, however, Muhammadsaw made it clear that the one to revive Islam would be of the Persian Lineage, as Ahmadas was:

حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ، عَنْ ثَوْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْغَيْثِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، رضى الله عنه قَالَ كُنَّا جُلُوسًا عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأُنْزِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ سُورَةُ الْجُمُعَةِ ‏{‏وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ‏}‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ مَنْ هُمْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ يُرَاجِعْهُ حَتَّى سَأَلَ ثَلاَثًا، وَفِينَا سَلْمَانُ الْفَارِسِيُّ، وَضَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدَهُ عَلَى سَلْمَانَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏”‏ لَوْ كَانَ الإِيمَانُ عِنْدَ الثُّرَيَّا لَنَالَهُ رِجَالٌ ـ أَوْ رَجُلٌ ـ مِنْ هَؤُلاَءِ ‏”‏‏.‏

Narrated Abu Huraira: While we were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) Surat Al-Jumu’a was revealed to him, and when the Verse, “And He (Allah) has sent him (Muhammad) also to other (Muslims)…..’ (62.3) was recited by the Prophet, I said, “Who are they, O Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ)?” The Prophet (ﷺ) did not reply till I repeated my question thrice. At that time, Salman Al-Farisi was with us. So Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) put his hand on Salman, saying, “If Faith were at (the place of) Ath-Thuraiya (pleiades, the highest star), even then a man from these people (i.e. Salman’s folk) would attain it.” (Bukhari, Volume 6, Book 60, Hadith #4897)

Another important point is that when Muhammadsaw mentions the Messiahasof the past, hesaw mentions him being in the company of the dead, who include Mosesas and Abrahamas, and when hesaw mentions the latter day messiahas, hesaw mentions its company with the living dajjal rather than the dead.

According to the most authentic book after the Qur’an known as Bukhari, the messiahs would not be the same person and they look different.

They say that because both Messiahs are said to resemble Urwa bin Masud, there is only one Messiah. There are many ways to approach this. Firstly, even if one hadith is proven to be weak, it would be sufficient as that would mean only one Messiah resembled Urwa bin Masud.

The second narration states:

فَيَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ كَأَنَّهُ عُرْوَةُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ

“Allah would send Isa Ibn Maryam (as) who would resemble Urwa bin Masud Sahih Muslim, Book of Tribulations and Portents of the Last Hour, Chapter : The Emergence of Dajjal…, Hadith #2940a

One of the narrators is Shu’bah bin al-Hajjaj and about him it is written:

كان يخطئ في أسماء الرجال كثيرا

“He would often err in the names of the narrators”

The second narrator is Ubaidullah bin Muadh al-Anbari about whom Ibn Mueen writes:

عن بن معين بن سمينة وشباب وعبيد الله بن معاذ ليسوا أصحاب حديث ليسوا بشيء

“Ibn Mumainah and Shahab and Ubaidullah bin Mu’adh were all unfamiliar with the science of Hadith and were incompetent narrators

Tahdhib-ut-Tahdhib, vol. 7, p. 49

As Ahmadi Muslims we agree that Hadrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (as) did in fact resemble Hadrat Isa (as) in appearance and in character. Allah the Almighty Revealed this to Hadrat Ahmad (as). Allah Stated:

أنت أشد مناسبةً بعيسى ابن مريم وأشبَهُ الناس به خُلقًا وخَلقًا وزمانًا

[Arabic] You have the closest relationship to ‘Isa Ibn-e-Maryam (as) [Jesus, son of Mary] and you are the nearest of all people to him in your qualities, your appearance, and the age in which you have been raised

Many resembled the Prophet Muhammad (sa) so why can’t two people resemble Hadrat Isa (as) of Bani Israel? Having some resemblance does not mean it is the same person. Ibn Hajr (rh) stated:

الَّذِينَ كَانُوا يُشَبَّهُونَ بِالنَّبِيِّ ﷺ غَيْرَ الْحَسَنِ وَالْحُسَيْنِ جَعْفَرُ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَابْنُهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ وَقُثَمُ بِالْقَافِ بن الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ وَأَبُو سُفْيَانَ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ وَمُسْلِمُ بْنُ عَقِيلِ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَمِنْ غَيْرِ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ السَّائِب بن يزِيد المطبي الْجَدُّ الْأَعْلَى لِلْإِمَامِ الشَّافِعِيِّ وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَامِرِ بْنِ كَرِيزٍ الْعَبْشَمِيُّ وَكَابِسُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ عَدِيٍّ فَهَؤُلَاءِ عَشَرَةٌ

“Those who resembled the Prophet (blessings and peace of Allah be upon him), other than al-Hasan and al-Husayn, were: Ja‘far ibn Abi Taalib and his son ‘Abdullah ibn Ja‘far, Qutham ibn al-‘Abbaas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Sufyaan ibn al-Haarith ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib and Muslim ibn ‘Aqeel ibn Abi Taalib. Among people other than Banu Haashim were: as-Saa’ib ibn Yazeed al-Muttalibi, the great-grandfather of Imam ash-Shaafa‘i, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Aamir ibn Kareez al-‘Abshami, and Kaabis ibn Rabee‘ah ibn ‘Adiyy. And these add up to ten (Fathul Bari, vol. 7, p. 97)

Ibn al-Jawzi (rh) writes:

وَكَانَ الْحسن شَدِيد الشّبَه برَسُول الله ﷺ. قَالَ أنس: لم يكن فيهم أحد أشبه بِالنَّبِيِّ ﷺ من الْحسن. وَمِمَّنْ كَانَ يشبه برَسُول الله جَعْفَر بن أبي طَالب، وَقثم بن الْعَبَّاس، وَأَبُو سُفْيَان بن الْحَارِث، والسائب بن عُبَيْدَة، وَكَانَ من التَّابِعين رجل يُقَال لَهُ كابس بن ربيعَة السَّامِي، من بني سامة بن لؤَي، كَانَ يُشبههُ، فَبعث إِلَيْهِ مُعَاوِيَة فَقبل بَين عَيْنَيْهِ، وأقطعه قطيعة، وَكَانَ أنس بن مَالك إِذا رَآهُ بَكَى.


… (continues on the website)

w17002.full:
The Testimony of Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (saw)

The Holy Prophet Muhammad(saw) quoted the verses, Surah Maidah verses 117-118 in regards to the condition of his sahaba and even quoted Isa(as) and falamma tawaffaitani as death relating his own death by the same words.

حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ، شَيْخٍ مِنَ النَّخَعِ عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ خَطَبَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏”‏ إِنَّكُمْ مَحْشُورُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ حُفَاةً عُرَاةً غُرْلاً ‏{‏كَمَا بَدَأْنَا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ‏}‏ ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ يُكْسَى يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِبْرَاهِيمُ، أَلاَ إِنَّهُ يُجَاءُ بِرِجَالٍ مِنْ أُمَّتِي، فَيُؤْخَذُ بِهِمْ ذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ، فَأَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَصْحَابِي فَيُقَالُ لاَ تَدْرِي مَا أَحْدَثُوا بَعْدَكَ فَأَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ ‏{‏وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا مَا دُمْتُ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏شَهِيدٌ‏}‏ فَيُقَالُ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ لَمْ يَزَالُوا مُرْتَدِّينَ عَلَى أَعْقَابِهِمْ مُنْذُ فَارَقْتَهُمْ ‏”‏‏.‏

Narrated Ibn `Abbas:

Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said, “O people! You will be gathered before Allah barefooted, naked and not circumcised.” Then (quoting Qur’an) he said:– “As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it. A promise We have undertaken: Truly we shall do it..” (21.104) The Prophet (ﷺ) then said, “The first of the human beings to be dressed on the Day of Resurrection, will be Abraham. Lo! Some men from my followers will be brought and then (the angels) will drive them to the left side (Hell-Fire). I will say. ‘O my Lord! (They are) my companions!’ Then a reply will come (from Almighty), ‘You do not know what they did after you.’ I will say as the pious slave (the Prophet (ﷺ) Jesus) said: And I was a witness over them while I dwelt amongst them. When You caused me to die. You were the Watcher over them and You are a Witness to all things.’ (5.117) Then it will be said, “These people have continued to be apostates since you left them.”(Sahih Bukhari Vol 6, Book 60, Hadith 149)

This further makes it clear that over here the word tawaffi means nothing other then death. Muhammad(saw) has made it clear with this Hadith.

Now it is important to talk about the word tawaffi because the non Ahmadis do not really understand the meaning. The word tawaffi is from waw fa ya and is the infinitive of the verb tawaffa. Whenever this appears in the form which is known as Bab Tafa’ul and the subject is Allah or the angels and them applying to a verb that has a soul it always means death (unless night or sleep is mentioned). It is always death when used for human beings, and the only part it is not death is when night or sleep is mentioned in the verse. Tawaffi is used in Al-Baqarah (2:235, 2:41), Al-e-‘Imran (3:194), Al-Nisa’ (4:16), Al-Nisa’ (4:98), Al-An‘am (6:62), Al-A‘raf (7:38), Al-A‘raf(7:127), Ar-Ra‘d (13:41), Yunus (10:47), Yusuf (12:102), Al-Nahl (16:33, 16:71), Al-Hajj (22:6), As-Sajdah (32:12), Az-Zumar (39:43), Al-Mu’min (40:68, 40:78), Muhammad (47:28), Al-An‘am (6:61), Al-Anfal (8:51), Yunus (10:105) and always means death except for in 6:61 and 39:43 because sleep or night are mentioned. In fact Allah Himself has told us when He causes tawaffa of a human being:

Allah states: “Allah takes away the souls of human beings at the time of their death; and during their sleep of those also that are not yet dead. And then He retains those against which He has decreed death, and sends back the others till an appointed term. In that surely are Signs for a people who reflect.” (Chapter 39 verse 43)

Now let us look at some Arabic dictionaries and see what they say about the word tawaffi.

Hadhrat Ibni Abbas(ra) a great companion made a statement which Imam Bukhari has quoted under the tafseer of Chapter 5 verses 117-118 :

“Ibni ‘Abbas (ra) states, ‘Mutawaffika means we caused you to die.’”( Sahih Bukhari, Kitabut-Tafsir, Surah Al-Ma’idah, Under the verse Falamma tawaffaitani..)

This clearly confirms what tawaffi means when used for a human being, and confirms that even when used for Isa(as) it means death. This statement is from a great sahaba which we cannot ignore.

Now to conclude the discussion on the meaning of tawaffi I will show the explanations from Lane’s lexicon, one of the most famous Arabic dictionaries:

Waw-Fa-Ya = to reach the end, keep ones promise, fulfil ones engagement, pay a debt, perform a promise. tawaffa – to die. wafaat – death.

Tawaffaa (prf 3rd. p. m. sing. V.): He causes to die.

Tawaffat (prf 3rd. p. f. sing. V.): They take away the soul.

Tawaffaitanii (prf. 2nd. p. m. sing. V.): ‘ou caused me to die.

Tatawaffaa (imp. 3rd.p.f.sing. V.): She causes to die.

Yatawaffaa (imp. 3rd. p. m. sing. V.): He causes to die.

Tawaffanii: Let me die; Let it be that I die.

Yutawaffaa (pp. 3rd. p. m. sing. V.): He has died.

Yutawaffauna (pip. 3rd. p. m. plu. V.): They die.

Mutawaffikka (ap-der. m. sing. V.): Cause you to die a natural death.

Some have tried claiming that when the word كَمَا is present it does not make the phrases the absolute same. No one claimed that the way Isa(As) died was 100% same to the Holy Prophet Muhammad(Saw) nor is their question they would be asked the same as the prophets mother was not worshiped. Tawaffa only occurs at death or sleep(when night or sleep is mentioned) are you now aware that kama is used in durood shareef? Are we not asking for blessings from the same God and the same blessings?This has no basis behind it as when kama is used it shows the resemblance between two things and the Holy Prophet Muhammad(saw) has made it clear that the resemblance is the exact same by quoting the exact same words of the ayah word for word. He could have changed them to show a resemblance but he showed that they are the exact same. Also in the Holy Qur’an we read:

“Surely, the case of Jesus with Allah is like the case of Adam. He created him out of dust, then He said to him, ‘Be!,’ and he was.” (Chapter 3 verse 60)

Now the word kama shows the resemblance between the two and the resemblance is the same. “Be and He was”

The words stated after kama kala for Muhammad(saw) are the exact same which Isa(as) will say on the day of judgment. Nowhere does it state it would be similar rather it is word for word the exact same.

كَمَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ ‏{وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ ۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَأَنْتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ}

This would be read till the end of the verse and clearly shows Isa(as) has died. After kama the exact same Arabic is used of the ayah which dictates the words of Isa(as) on the day of Judgment. The Holy Prophet(saw) made it clear that his words would be exactly the same.

Kala shows the resemblance of two things and if different the Prophet(saw) would have clarified as the examples the non Ahmadis quote have different explanations after kama. The hadith we quote is exactly word for word, what isa(as) will say on the day of judgment and therefore the words are exactly the same which the Prophet(saw) will say and their tawaffa is also the same.

Challenge of the Promised Messiah (as) Regarding Tawaffi

He(as) states: “If anyone can cite a single instance from the Holy Qur’an or Hadith, or from ancient or modern Arabic poetry and prose, that the word Tawaffi, when applied to a human being, God being the subject, has been used in any connotation other than death and taking possession of the soul, for instance, in the connotation of the taking the body, I bind myself on oath that I shall pay that person one thousand rupees in cash by selling some of my property and shall always hold him in high esteem as a great scholar of the HolyQur’an and Hadith.”(Izalah-e-Auham, Ruhani Khaza’in, Volume 3, p. 603)

Another Statement of Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad(as) :

“What I discovered on checking every page of the compilations of Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Tirmadhi, Ibn-e-Majah, Abu Dawud, Nasa’i, Darimi, Mu’atta’ and Sharh-us-Sunnah etc., was that the expression Tawaffi has been used three hundred and forty six times, and in no single instance has it been used, either by the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) or by his companions, to mean anything other than ‘death’, or ‘taking possession of the soul’. I have gone through these books with great care line by line, and I can say that on each and every occasion the expression Tawaffi has been used only in the connotation of death or taking possession of the soul.” [Izala-e-Auham, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 3, pp. 583-585]

w19339.full:
Most of us are aware of the issues surrounding Hamza Ali Abbasi for his courageous question in regards to protecting minorities, which is from the sunnah of the Holy Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم). First it is important to understand why Hamza Ali has faced so much backlash by extreme religious clerics, or in other words Mullahs in Pakistan. We should not be surprised by this as the condition of these scholars was actually prophesied by the Holy Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) in regards to the end times. Here are three important ahadith which illustrate the conditions of the end times:

‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، قَالَ كُنَّا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَشَخَصَ بِبَصَرِهِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏”‏ هَذَا أَوَانٌ يُخْتَلَسُ الْعِلْمُ مِنَ النَّاسِ حَتَّى لاَ يَقْدِرُوا مِنْهُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ ‏”‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ زِيَادُ بْنُ لَبِيدٍ الأَنْصَارِيُّ كَيْفَ يُخْتَلَسُ مِنَّا وَقَدْ قَرَأْنَا الْقُرْآنَ فَوَاللَّهِ لَنَقْرَأَنَّهُ وَلَنُقْرِئَنَّهُ نِسَاءَنَا وَأَبْنَاءَنَا ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏”‏ ثَكِلَتْكَ أُمُّكَ يَا زِيَادُ إِنْ كُنْتُ لأَعُدُّكَ مِنْ فُقَهَاءِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ هَذِهِ التَّوْرَاةُ وَالإِنْجِيلُ عِنْدَ الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى فَمَاذَا تُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ

Narrated Jubair bin Nufair: from Abu Ad-Darda who said: “We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he raised his sight to the sky,
then he said: ‘This is the time when knowledge is to be taken from the people, until what remains of it shall not amount to anything.” So Ziyad bin Labid Al-Ansari said: ‘How will it be taken from us while we recite the Qur’an. By Allah we recite it, and our women and children recite it?’ He (ﷺ) said: ‘May you be bereaved of your mother O Ziyad! I used to consider you among the Fuqaha of the people of Al-Madinah. The Tawrah and Injil are with the Jews and Christians, but what do they avail of them?'” (Jami’ at-Tirmidhi Hadith #2653)

عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه، قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:”يوشك أن أو سيأتي على الناس زمان لا يبقى من الإسلام إلا اسمه، ولا يبقى من القرآن إلا رسمه، مساجدهم يومئذ عامرة وهي خراب من الهدى، علماؤهم شر من تحت أديم السماء، منهم أو من عندهم خرجت أو تخرج أو يمدح الفتنة وفيهم تعود“

‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib (ra) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (sa) said: “A time will come in the near future when there will be nothing left of the Islam except its name. And there will be nothing left of the Holy Qur’ān except its words. The mosques of that age will apparently be full of people, but will be empty of righteousness. Their ‘Ulamā’ will be the worst creatures under the heaven. Discourse will rise from them and will come right back to them.”(Mishkat Kitabul Ilm)

حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الدِّمَشْقِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ بَكْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ جَابِرٍ، حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو عَبْدِ السَّلاَمِ، عَنْ ثَوْبَانَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏”‏ يُوشِكُ الأُمَمُ أَنْ تَدَاعَى عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا تَدَاعَى الأَكَلَةُ إِلَى قَصْعَتِهَا ‏”‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ قَائِلٌ وَمِنْ قِلَّةٍ نَحْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ قَالَ ‏”‏ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ كَثِيرٌ وَلَكِنَّكُمْ غُثَاءٌ كَغُثَاءِ السَّيْلِ وَلَيَنْزِعَنَّ اللَّهُ مِنْ صُدُورِ عَدُوِّكُمُ الْمَهَابَةَ مِنْكُمْ وَلَيَقْذِفَنَّ اللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمُ الْوَهَنَ ‏”‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ قَائِلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا الْوَهَنُ قَالَ ‏”‏ حُبُّ الدُّنْيَا وَكَرَاهِيَةُ الْمَوْتِ ‏”‏ ‏.‏

Narrated Thawban: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: The people will soon summon one another to attack you as people when eating invite others to share their dish. Someone asked: Will that be because of our small numbers at that time? He replied: No, you will be numerous at that time: but you will be scum and rubbish like that carried down by a torrent, and Allah will take fear of you from the breasts of your enemy and last enervation into your hearts. Someone asked: What is wahn (enervation). Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): He replied: Love of the world and dislike of death (Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith #4297)

As a result of this incident on Hamza Ali’s show, there has been a storm of misinformation regarding the life and character of Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (عليه السلام), the Promised Messiah and Mahdi.Hazrat Ahmad (عليه السلام) was born in 1835 in Qadian, a small town in India. He was a true devotee of Islam from the onset of his life, and defended the Holy Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) like none other. The Holy Qur`an makes it clear that Prophets have already lived a life before you, and that after making their claim people turn their backs. We see this in the life of the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) as well. In the case of Ahmad (عليه السلام), one of his arch enemies, Mohammad Hussain Batalvi said in regards to a book written by Ahmad (عليه السلام)

“In our opinion, this book in this age, and to meet the present circumstances, is such that the like of it has not been written up to this time in Islam … its author, too, has proved himself to be firmly staunch in helping the cause of Islam with his money, with his pen and his tongue, and with his personal religious experiences.” (Ishaat-us-Sunnah, Vol. 7, June-November 1884)

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (عليه السلام) gained lots of popularity in India as he was the only one defending Islam to such an extent that the scholars themselves understood that none other can defend Islam to the extent of which he did. He had many debates with different religions and he became well known after his debate with Abdullah Atham, who wrote extensively against Islam. The Promised Messiah (عليه السلام) among many of his debates, was never defeated. Here is a statement from an Anti Ahmadi himself who was forced to agree: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IMaKaosL0cI

On one occasion Maulvi Irshad Ali of Nagpur said,“The Christian missionary Safdur Ali has challenged me to a debate with him on the truth of Islam and Christianity. … But I can ask him that if he is so confident about his arguments and the truth of Christianity, where was he when Maulavi Ghulam Ahmad Qadiani stood in the field of debate like a brave lion and challenged him. This challenge had such an effect on you people that no Christian missionary dare confront him [Mirza Ghulam Ahmad].” (Magazine Dastkari, Amritsar, 18 June 1899)

He received his first divine revelation in the year of 1869 and his first book was published in the year of 1880.
He (عليه السلام) claimed to be appointed by God as the reviver of the faith in the year 1882, and the first initiation of his community took place in 1889. As we see from the history of all prophets, they have made gradual claims as God has revealed to them. For example, at first the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) was told that he should warn only his near relatives. Much later, God told him that he is a messenger to all of mankind. In the start, Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was not told that he was best of Prophets, rather it was much later when it was revealed to him that he was Khataman Nabiyeen, the seal of the prophets. The Holy Qur’an states that prophets speak only when Allah commands them (Chapter 21, Verse 28), and just as such, the Promised Messiah (عليه السلام) said only what God revealed to him about his status.

From the start, the Promised Messiah (as) got revelation that he was a Nabi, but only interpreted it in different ways as those days it was popularly spread that all Prophets bring new teachings. Introduction:

An allegation that has been raised against the founder of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community, Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian (as), is that he stated that he would live to an age around 80 years but the age at which he passed away was far off this. However. this is far from the truth.

Chronology of Revelations:

ProphecyInterpretationReference

ثمانين حولا أو قريبا من ذلكEighty years or near that.Izala-e-Auham, Ruhani Khazain, vol. 3, p 443 (1891)

ProphecyYears Specified by AllahReference

یری عمر اسی برس کی ہوگی اور یا یہ کہ پانچ چھ سال زیادہ یا پانچ چھ سال کم اور جو ظاہر الفاظ وحی کے وعدہ کے متعلق ہیں وہ تو اسی برس سے بھی عمر زیادہ ہوسکتی ہے اور جو ظاہر الفاظ وحی کے وعدہ کے متعلق ہیں وہ چہتر اور چھیاسی کے اندر عمر کی تعیین کرتےGod had informed me in clear terms that I would live to the age of eighty, or that five to six years more or five to six years less. Nor is there a promise of God that my age will necessarily exceed eighty years. Rather, the hope implied in the words in the revelation of God is that, if God so desires, my age could even somewhat exceed eighty years. The actual words of the Revelation that pertain to this promise, however, fix the age between 74 and 86.Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya, Part 5, Ruhani Khazain, vol. 21, p. 258-259 (1905)

اطال الله بقاءك اسی یا اس پر پانچ چار زیادہ ای پانچ چار کمAllah will prolong your life. Eighty years—four or five more, or four or five less.Haqiqatul Wahi, Ruhani Khazain, vol. 22, p. 100 (1907)

Table of revelations regarding the age of the Promised Messiah

From this we can see that the prophecy stated that the Promised Messiah (as) as living eight years, a few years more or a few years less. However, the actual words specified it to be between 74-86. In another prophecy in Haqiqatul Wahi, the very words of the prophecy specify it being four or five years less or four or five years more. This leads us to between 75-85 years. Now it is to be understood that while two of the references could be construed to mean that the Promised Messiah (as) thought he would live for more than 80 years, this is implausible as the prophecies which they refer to states around 80 and interpretations given before those writings and after those writings state that this could be a few years less or a few years more. In addition, in Barahin e Ahmadiyya he specifies that it is not necessary that he lives to 80 years. Therefore, the rational conclusion is that the Promised Messiah (as) was summarising the prophecy as he demonstrated in Barahin e Ahmadiyya what the actual words of the Prophecy entail.

Estimations Are Uncertain:

It is argued that the Promised Messiah (as) was born in 1839 instead of the traditionally accepted 1835. However, it must be understood that references from the Promised Messiah (as) can be used to support many dates. However, this is due to the fact that people during his time would estimate their age and so their estimations wouldn’t necessarily be a correct depiction what was the case but would precisely be what they are; estimations and nothing more and nothing less. This can be confirmed from the Promised Messiah (as) where he states that nobody knows his true age except Allah (swt):

“Only Allah Knows my real age, but according to my knowledge, my age is near 70 years in this year of 1323 and Allah Knows Best”

[Ruhani Khazain Volume 21, Barahin-e- Ahmadiyya Volume 5, Page 325]

Evidence that is used to prove that Hazrat Ahmad (as) was born past 1835:

1836:

“I spent almost 40 years of my life under the protection of my father.”

[Ruhani Khazain, vol. 13, pg. 195]

Hazrat Ahmad (as) states that he spent almost 40 years with his father. His father passed away in 1876 so this would take us to 1836. However, since it is an estimation it is not precise.

1839/1840:

“I was born in 1839 or 1840, in the twilight of the Sikh rule, and was in my sixteenth or seventeenth year in 1857…”

[Kitab al-Bariyya, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 13, p. 177]

However, this is clearly an estimate as he states 1839 OR 1840. In addition, he states he was in his sixteenth or seventeenth year in 1857 but according to the two years quoted (1839 or 1840) he would have been seventeen or eighteen. This demonstrates that these were the estimations of the Promised Messiah (as). Furthermore, it states the birth was in the twilight of the Sikh rule while in the same book it states that his father had suffered huge hardships before his birth but when he was born these had ended. This could not have been the case in 1839 as that is when Ranjit Singh had died and the hardships ending referred to the return of land (more on this in the coming section).

1841:

“God Almighty is witness that I will tell the truth – my age is around sixty years”

[Malfuzat Volume II pg. 187]

This was taken in 1901 which suggests that he may have been born in 1841. However, this is also an estimate as it says around sixty years (which could include 65).

1844:

“By this calculation, my birth took place when out of the six thousand years, eleven years remained”

[Footnote Tohfa-e-Golharviyya pg.135]

Hazrat Ahmad was informed through Kashf that there were 4739 years between Adam (as) and the death of the Prophet Muhammad (saw)). He calculated from his own that he was born 11 years before 6000 (5889) which would be 1260AH and consequently the year 1844.

Firstly, as we can see this is a calculation that Hazrat Ahmad (as) made and not part of the revelation. Secondly, even the opponents couldn’t accept this as it would contradict their 1839 date and be vastly inconsistent with the evidence. The issue with the calculation was that 1250 Hijri years were added to the 4739 years, resulting in a total of 5889. However, this is a common error as 1250 should have been added to 4728/4729 instead since 4739 is when the Prophet (saw) passed away and is not (as commonly misunderstood) the beginning of the Hijri calendar. Under this new calculation we would get a total of 5878/5879.

Evidence that is used to prove that Hazrat Ahmad (as) was born before 1835:

1833:

“I published an announcement in English on 23 August 1903, opposing Mr. Dowie. It says; ‘I am about seventy years in age and Mr. Dowie, as he states, is a young man of fifty but I do not care for my age because this mubahalah will not be decided by our ages but God who is the Most Supreme Authority will decide it.”

[Haqiqatul Wahi, 639]

1834:

“If Atham is sixty-four years of age, this humble self is around sixty…”

[Majmu’a Ishtiharat, vol. 2, pg 62]

Evidence that is used to prove that Hazrat Ahmad (as) was born in 1835:

“Then when I reached the age of forty, God honoured me with his revelation and word.”

[Tiryaqul Quloob, pg.283]

“It is amazing—and I consider this to be a Sign of God—that I was blessed with converse and discourse with God Almighty exactly in the year 1290 Hijrah – seven years thereafter, Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya—in which my claim is recorded-was compiled and published.”

[Haqiqatul Wahi, Ruhani Khazain, vol. 22, p. 208]

This demonstrates that the Promised Messiah (as) was forty years old when he received revelation and that was in the year 1290 Hijrah. That would mean he was born in 1250AH which corresponds to 1835. This is further confirmed by the fact that it says Barahin e Ahmadiyya was published around 7 years after he was blessed with converse. This would give us around 1874-1875. This is further confirmed by Barahin e Ahmadiyya part 5 in 1905, in which it states that he had been chosen around 30 years ago (1874-1875). This would make the Promised Messiah (as) 40 at the time of the appointment and 73 when he passed away (75 lunar years).

Methodology to Determine True Age:

As we can see due to the variety of estimations there needs to be a way in which one can objectively determine the age of the Promised Messiah (as). This can be done as we know three facts:

• He was born on a Friday.

• He was born on the 14th of a lunar month.

• He was born in the Hindu calendar month of Phagun

The first two are mentioned by himself:

“This humble one was born on a Friday, on the 14th night of the moon”

[Tohfa-e-Golarhviyya pg. 281]

The last one was mentioned by his companion, Mufti Muhammad Sadiq (rh):

“His Holiness the Promised Messiah (as) at one time mentioned that the month in which he was born was the month of Phagun”

[Zikre Habib pg.189]

When we put these facts together, two prominent dates emerge:

Now in order to determine which one is the better candidate, we turn to the works of Hazrat Ahmad (as). There is indeed another criteria:

“And I heard my mother repeatedly say to me: ‘our days have been changed since the day you were born, and we were before in hardships and misfortunes and in all kinds of anguish and tribulations, so all good things have come to us with your coming and you are among the blessed ones. My father was ascending from one rank to another, and from one high to the next, until he ascended to the ascents of progress and god bestowed on him a garment of honour and reverence and nothing befell him and he became of the wealthy”

[Aine Kamalat e Islam, 1893 p. 544]

From this we find that before Hazrat Ahmad (as) was born, his family was in difficulty but after his birth, their prosperity began and his father began ascending from rank to rank. Now what was the nature of this ascendance?

Lepel Griffin, a British administrator and diplomat, who had been appointed Chief Secretary of the Punjab from 1880, penned a famous work called ‘The Panjab Chiefs’.

In his book, he mentions that the family of the Promised Messiah (as) were poor until Mirza Ghulam Murtaza (his father) received a ‘large portion of his ancestral estates’. Griffin goes on to write “He (Mirza Ghulam Murtaza) then entered the army of the Maharaja and performed efficient service on the Kashmir frontier and at other places.” This shows that after he received his land and his fortunes returned, he fought for Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Now we can analyse which battles Maharaja Ranjit Singh had commanded:

This shows that the last battle was in 1837. This consequently eliminates the 1839 date, allowing us to definitively conclude with the fact that the Promised Messiah (as) was born on Friday 13th February 1835.

Fulfilment:

To reach an age above 50 was considered extremely rare. It was even more unlikely to live past 60:

“It is a pity that such people are not mindful of death. Is death a far off thing? A person who has reached the age of fifty will live perhaps for a few more years, or ten years at most; ultimately, he must die.”

[Malfuzat – Volume III pg.76-77]

The life expectancy in British India at the time was around 25 years, making it extremely remarkable to live into one’s 70s.

The Promised Messiah (as) was born on Friday 13th February 1835, living a life of 73 solar years and 75 lunar years, consequently fulfilling the prophecy he had made decades before. This was remarkable that a man in an area where life expectancy was low and the percentage of individuals who exceeded 60 years old were minimal, prophesied that he would live to at least 74/75 years and God kept him alive to fulfil the prophecy. He would have multiple illnesses, partake in prayer duels, be the victim of assassination attempts, yet none of this could prevent the fulfilment of his prophecy. After all, how could anyone stop what God has willed to occur. As his famous opponent, Sanaullah Amritsari testifies:

“Mirza Sahib has said that his demise would be near 80 years of age and perhaps he has fulfilled all those conditions”

[Ahl-e-hadith 3rd May 1907 page 3 Column 2]

Conclusion:

During the time of the Promised Messiah, people would estimate their ages. Having stated that only God knows his true age, he had several estimations. From those estimations two years emerged as viable: 1835 and 1839. Given objective historical information from the Chief of the Punjab, the latter was ruled out. As the words of the Prophecy meant that the Promised Messiah (as) would live between 74/75-85/86, he lived an age of 75 years, consequently fulfilling an extremely improbable prophecy given his circumstances. This ended up not falsifying his truthfulness but rather vindicating it.

Introduction

The Book of Revelation, also known as the Apocalypse or the Apocalypse of John, is traditionally attributed to the Apostle John, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus. Yet when examined historically, the question of its authorship is far less certain. The author identifies himself simply as “John” and does not identify himself as the Apostle John. Moreover, differences in language, style, theology, and historical context have led many modern scholars to distinguish the author of Revelation from the apostle traditionally associated with the Gospel of John and the Johannine letters.

Islam teaches that God originally revealed the Injil to Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). Muslims do not, however, regard the present New Testament as identical to that original revelation. Rather, it contains a collection of writings produced and transmitted by human beings after Jesus, alongside material believed to preserve elements of his original teaching.

The Book of Revelation is one of the New Testament’s most influential books and its final book. Yet if its traditional attribution to the Apostle John cannot be established, and scholars question who actually wrote it, this raises an important point from an Islamic perspective. It highlights the distinction between the original revelation given by God to a prophet and later writings produced by people about that prophet and his teachings. It also stands in contrast to the Quran, which has been preserved in its original Arabic language and transmitted as a single, standardized scripture since the time of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

Below are testimonies from Christian historians, scholars, and commentaries who question who the actual author of the Book of Revelation was.

Eusebius Pamphilus (260-340 AD)

Early Christian scholar and bishop Eusebius Pamphilus, also known as the “Father of Church History,” wrote in his historical account of early Christianity that the author of Revelation was not the Apostle John.

“I do not, therefore, deny that he was called John, and that this was the writing of one John. And I agree that it was the work, also, of some holy and inspired man. But I would not easily agree that this was the apostle, the son of Zebedee, the brother of James, who is the author of the gospel, and the general (catholic) epistle that bears his name. But I conjecture, both from the general tenor of both, and the form and complexion of the composition, and the execution of the whole book, that it is not from him.”

[The Ecclesiastical history of Eusebius Pamphilus, A Historical Review, p. 208]

Bernard Orchard (Catholic)

A British Catholic monk notes that scholars have debated for centuries which “John” the Book of Revelation should be attributed to. He shows support for the view of Eusebius, who suggested that John the Presbyter, not John the Apostle, may have been its author, and even questioned whether Revelation should have been included in the New Testament at all.

“[…] Eusebius however (HE iv, 13, 8) says that either the book must be ranked as among the undisputed NT books or rejected as apocryphal, and suggests that its author might be John the Presbyter mentioned by Papias. This ‘other’ John might account for the story of the ‘two tombs’.

[A Catholic Commentary on Holy Scripture, The Apocalypse] [Enlarged Page Scan]

Peter S. Williamson

Scholar Peter S. Williamson notes difficulties in identifying the author of Revelation as the Apostle John or the writer of the Gospel and Letters attributed to him, highlighting key differences in style and authorship.

“However, there are some difficulties in identifying the author of Revelation with John the apostle or with the author of the Gospel and Letters that bear his name. First, the author of Revelation never refers to himself as an apostle but indicates he is a prophet (1:3) and a brother among the prophets (22:9), a group he distinguishes from the apostles (18:20). When Revelation speaks of the twelve apostles of the Lamb as the foundation stones of the wall of the new Jerusalem (21:14), there is no suggestion that the author includes himself in their number.”

[Scan: Catholic Commentary on Sacred Scripture by Peter S. Williamson, Author Section]

He further notes that several prominent Eastern Church Fathers — Cyril, Gregory, Eusebius, and Theodoret — did not believe the Apostle John wrote Revelation or even considered it part of Scripture due to its very problematic interpretations. At the end, he acknowledges that, unless new evidence emerges, the true author of Revelation cannot be known with certainty.

“Other prominent Church Fathers in the East – including Cyril of Jerusalem, Gregory of Nazianzus, John Chrysostom, Eusebius, and Theodoret – did not consider the apostle John the author of Revelation or even regard it as part of the canon of Scripture. Some of their uneasiness was due to problematic interpretations of the book and to the use made of it by the Montanists, members of a heretical early Christian sect.

The striking style differences noted by Dionysius continue to persuade most scholars that the author of Revelation was not the same person who wrote the Gospel and Epistles of John. However, some scholars maintain that the apostle John did write Revelation and explain the stylistic differences as due to the book’s apocalyptic genre, or to the apostle John’s use of a secretary (an amanuensis) in the composition of his other books, not available to him on Patmos.

Unless new information is uncovered, we cannot know for sure who wrote Revelation. […]”
[Scan: Catholic Commentary on Sacred Scripture by Peter S. Williamson, Author Section]

[Scan: Catholic Commentary on Sacred Scripture by Peter S. Williamson, Author Section]

Zaine Ridling

Zaine Ridling, Ph.D., notes that while some early sources, like Justin Martyr, attributed Revelation to the Apostle John, the book’s internal evidence remains inconclusive.

“[…] Although some ancient authorities (e.g., Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 81.4) have suggested that this is the apostle John, the son of Zebedee (see Mk 3.17), the internal evidence of the book itself is inconclusive.“

[The Bible, Revelation Introduction, p.539]

He goes on to list some historical context and concludes that the traditional identification of Revelation’s author with the Apostle John is questionable.

“[…] The traditional identification of the John of the book of Revelation with the apostle of the same name is thus questionable.”

[The Bible, Revelation Introduction, p.539-540]

Charles T. Chapman (Baptist)

Christian Baptist theologian Charles T. Chapman, Jr. also arrives at a similar conclusion:

B. Who Wrote the Book, When Was It Written, and Who Were Its First Readers?

Questions concerning the author, date, and first recipients of Revelation seem easy compared to the task of deciphering the book’s symbols. However, the question of authorship in particular is rather tricky. In 1:1, 4, and 9 the author identifies himself as John. The question is, which John? The John whom most people immediately think of, the one tradition says wrote the book, is St. John the Apostle. However, the traditional title of the book is not “The Revelation of St. John the Apostle,” but “St. John the Divine.” “Divine” means “seer,” that is, one who is granted a vision of the future. […]

Any other discussion of the identity of the author of Revelation is only so much educated guesswork.

Suffice it to say that the writer is closely associated with the same group of people that gave us the Gospel of John and the Letters of John and had their headquarters in Ephesus. We will go ahead and call the author of Revelation “John” even though there is much uncertainty about who he was.“

[The Message of the Book of Revelation by Charles T. Chapman, Jr., p.7-8]

Michael P. Barber

A professor of Sacred Scripture, theology, & Catholic thought, he also states that the identity of ‘John’ is unknown and lists several early Christian scholars who were proponents of the “other John theory” of authorship.

HOLY GHOST WRITER

Who Wrote the Apocalypse and When?
Will the Real John Please Stand Up?

” […] But who is this John the Revelator, who authored the Book of Revelation? Some modern scholars challenge the notion that John was the “revelator.” Others, while agreeing that John is the author, disagree as to the identity of this John. Was it John the Apostle, or was there another John who merely shared the same name?“

[Unlocking the Book of Revelation, Who Wrote the Apocalypse and When, p.1]

Ignatius Catholic Study Bible

The Ignatius Catholic Study Bible notes that while tradition links Revelation to the Apostle John, this has been questioned since the 3rd century. Dionysius of Alexandria and modern scholars reject this view due to differences in style and themes.

” Four times the author of Revelation calls himself “John” (1:1, 4, 9; 22:8). He claims to be living in exile on the island of Patmos (1:9), where he received heavenly visions along with instructions to record them in a book (1:11,19; 2:1, etc.). Christian tradition generally identifies him as the Apostle John, son of Zebedee (Mk 3:17) and the reputed author of the Gospel and epistles of John. Testimony supporting the apostolic authorship of Revelation comes from an array of ancient writers, including St. Justin Martyr (A.D. 165), St. Irenaeus (A.D. 180), St. Clement of Alexandria (A.D. 200), St. Hippolytus (A.D. 225), and St. Athanasius (ca. A.D. 350).

It must be noted, however, that this majority report is not the only report to have come down to us from Christian antiquity. Skepticism about whether the Apostle John authored the Book of Revelation surfaced in the middle of the third century, when Dionysius of Alexandria argued that the Greek idiom of Revelation differs so markedly from the other writings of John that it could not have been penned by the same author. He also noted that several key concepts in John’s writings are absent from Revelation (e.g., life, truth, grace, joy) and that this absence weighs against a common authorship of Revelation and the other NT books attributed to the apostle (for the arguments of Dionysius, see Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History 7, 25). Most modern scholars agree with this assessment and therefore discount the tradition that connects Revelation to John the Apostle.

[Scan: Ignatius Catholic Study Bible, Introduction to The Revelation To Saint John, p.1]

Oxford Bible Commentary

The Oxford Bible Commentary states that the author of Revelation was a Christian prophet named John, who was exiled on Patmos. While John was a common name at the time, there is no reason to identify him with the Apostle John.

“B. Author and Date. The author of Revelation was a Christian prophet named John (1:1, 4; 22:8), of whom we know only that he was familiar with the Christian communities in the Roman province of Asia and at the time of writing was exiled on the island of Patmos. John was one of the most common of Jewish names in the period, and there is no reason to identify him with the apostle John, though this identification was made. […]”

[THE OXFORD BIBLE COMMENTARY, Revelation, p.1288]

New Oxford Annotated Bible

The New Oxford Annotated Bible states that while some early sources suggested Revelation was written by the Apostle John the internal evidence is inconclusive. It also questions the connection between the John of Revelation and the Apostle or the author of the Gospel and Letters.

“While some ancient authorities (e.g. Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 814) suggested that this is the apostle John, the son of Zebedee (see Mk 3.17), internal evidence from the book itself is inconclusive. […] The traditional identification of the John of the book of Revelation with the apostle of the same name is thus highly questionable, as is the connection of the John of the book of Revelation with the Gospel According to John or with the Letters of John.”

[THE NEW OXFORD ANNOTATED BIBLE, The Revelation to John, p. 2153]

Chronological Study Bible

The Chronological Study Bible notes that a debate continues over whether the author of Revelation is John the Apostle, John the Elder, or an otherwise unknown John.

“In the 3rd century these variations of the original language prompted scholars to question the apostle John’s authorship of the Revelation. A debate still continues over whether the John who wrote this book is to be identified is to be identified with John the apostle. John the Elder (see “The First Letter of John” at 1 John 1:1), or an otherwise unknown John.”

[Chronological Study Bible, p.1408]

The New International Commentary on the New Testament

The New International Commentary on the New Testament states that within the Book of Revelation itself, there is no specific indication as to who exactly the author John was. The Commentary lists several suggestions from historical works and speculations about who John may have been, including John the Prophet, a young man, and others.

“Within the book itself, however, there is no specific indication as to who exactly this John was. […]”

[Scan: The New International Commentary on the New Testament THE BOOK OF REVELATION REVISED, Authorship]

It then further asks:

“Who, then, was the John who wrote Revelation?’ Internal evidence has led most scholars to conclude that, whoever he was, there is little possibility that he was also the author of the Fourth Gospel.”

[Scan: The New International Commentary on the New Testament THE BOOK OF REVELATION REVISED, Authorship]

The Expositor’s Bible Commentary

The Expositor’s Bible Commentary notes that during the Reformation, questions about Revelation’s authorship and canon resurfaced. Luther, offended by its content, called it ‘neither apostolic nor prophetic,’ and the authorship issue remains problematic.

“The Reformation period witnessed a renewal of the earlier questions concerning its apostolic authorship and canonical status. Thus Luther, offended by the contents of Revelation, declared that he regarded it as “neither apostolic nor prophetic.” […] To sum up, the question of authorship is problematic.”

[Scan: THE EXPOSITOR’S BIBLE COMMENTARY by Kenneth Barker & John Kohlenberger, Authorship section]

Catholic bible press

This New Revised Standardized Version (NRSV) Bible copy suggests that the author of Revelation is probably not John the Apostle, but rather a disciple of his or another Christian leader who claimed to be living in exile on the island of Patmos.

“The author is probably not John the Apostle, but a disciple of his or another Christian leader who claimed to be living in exile on the island of Patmos.”

[The Holy Bible NRSV, Catholic Bible Press, Introduction: The Revelation to John]

The Jerusalem Bible

The Jerusalem Bible states that it is impossible to identify the author of Revelation..

“[…] Internal evidence shows that the Revelation of John has some affinity with the other Johannine writings, but as it is so sharply distinguished from them by language, style, and some theological positions, notably its view of the parcusia, it is impossible to identify the author of Revelation with the author of the rest of the Johannine literature.”

[The Jerusalem Bible, Introduction to the Book of Revelation, p.427-428]

The Bible Dictionary

The Bible Dictionary states that nothing in Revelation links the author to John the son of Zebedee or John the Elder. Sound judgment leads to the conclusion that the author is a John otherwise unknown to us.

“Author: Although the author never claims directly to be a prophet, several passages suggest such was his self-understanding (e.g., 22:9). He calls himself John (1:4). Nothing in the work links the author to John the son of Zebedee or John the Elder. Sound judgment requires the conclusion that he is a John otherwise unknown to us.”

[The Bible Dictionary by Paul J. Achtemeier, Revelation to John, p. 931]

Reading the Book of Revelation

In ‘Reading the Book of Revelation’, it states that most Christian scholars today are fully certain that the Book of Revelation was written by an unknown prophet named John and not by John the Apostle, the disciple of Jesus.

“Thus important preliminary questions include: Who wrote Revelation? When? Where? And why was it written in this form? While individual scholars may disagree on one or another detail, most today are convinced that the Book of Revelation was written in the form of an apocalypse (more in a moment) by an otherwise unknown prophet named John, who traveled through the cities of Asia Minor in the late first century. Although tradition identified this John with John the apostle, the disciple of Jesus, this is unlikely. […]”

[Reading the Book of Revelation, A Resource for Students, p. 4]

Conclusion

Ultimately, academic findings like this that question biblical authorship serve as historical evidence that is consistent with what the Holy Quran claimed 1,400 years ago: that the scriptures of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) underwent human editing and lack a direct, unbroken chain of transmission back to their divine origins.

Questions for Christians

1. If we cannot establish who actually wrote Revelation, on what basis should it be accepted as authoritative Scripture?

2. Why was Revelation traditionally attributed to the Apostle John when the book itself never identifies its author as John the Apostle?

3. If there are multiple theories about who this “John” was—including John the Apostle, John the Presbyter, a prophet, or another otherwise unknown John—how can Christians be certain which person actually wrote it?

4. If prominent Christian scholars and Church Fathers themselves questioned the authorship and even the canonical status of Revelation, why should its inclusion in the New Testament be considered unquestionable?

5. If the Apostle John did not write Revelation, why should the authority of an anonymous or otherwise unknown author be placed on the same level as direct revelation given to a prophet of God?

6. If the authorship of biblical books can become uncertain over time, how can Christians be certain that the New Testament today represents exactly what was originally revealed to Jesus?

7. If God intended His revelation to serve as guidance for humanity, why would its original form, authorship, and transmission become matters of historical uncertainty?

Introduction

It is a prevalent belief amongst the non-Ahmadi Muslims, especially the ‘Sunnis’, that when the Messiah comes, he will fight Gog and Magog through supernatural powers granted to him by Allah the Almighty. This is not only shirk but goes against the true prophecy of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

Gog and Magog Cannot be Fought by Anyone

The Holy Prophet (SAW) clearly stated that in the latter days, Gog and Magog would gain such dominance that no worldly power would be able to resist them, not even the Messiah or Mahdi (AS). This is described in the Hadith below:

This hadith has been narrated on the authority of Jabir with the same chain of transmitters but with this addition that Gog and Magog would walk until they would reach the mountain of al-Khamar and it is a mountain of Bait-ul-Maqdis and they would say:

“We have killed those who are upon the earth. Let us now kill those who are In the sky and they would throw their arrows towards the sky and the arrows would return to them besmeared with blood. And in the narration of Ibn Hujr (the words are):” I have sent such persons (Gog and Magog) that none would dare fight against them.“

[Sahih Muslim 2937b]

Messiah Will Take His People to the Mountain

But the Prophet (SAW) did not leave us hopeless. He also told us the exact remedy the Messiah would use, and would teach his Jama’ah to use as well: taking his people to the mountains and turning completely to Allah in prayer. According to the Prophet (SAW), these were the only remedies that would work against the massive influence of Gog and Magog in the latter times. This is described in the Ahadith below:

“[…] He will then search for Dajjal until he will catch hold of him at the gate of Ludd (village near Jerusalem), and will kill him. Then the people, whom Allah will have protected, will come to `Isa son of Maryam, and he will wipe their faces and will inform them of their ranks in Jannah, and it will be under such conditions that Allah will reveal to `Isa these words: `I have brought forth from amongst my slaves such people against whom none will be able to fight, so take these people safely to the mountain […]”
[Riyad as-Salihin 1808]

أَوْحَى اللَّهُ إِلَى عِيسَى إِنِّي قَدْ أَخْرَجْتُ عِبَادًا لِي لاَ يَدَانِ لأَحَدٍ بِقِتَالِهِمْ فَحَرِّزْ عِبَادِي إِلَى الطُّورِ ‏۔ وَيَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ وَهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُونَ۔۔۔

“Allah would send a revelation to [the Promised] Jesus (AS) that, ‘I have brought forth such people, against whom no one has the power to fight; so you take my people safely to the mount Tur (Sinai). Then Allah would send Gog and Magog and they would hasten forth from every height…”

[Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan] [Hadith snapshot]

Allah SWT instructing the Messiah to “seek shelter on a mountain” is not to be taken literally. Rather, it is a metaphor which emphasizes the following:

• detachment from material fears

• reliance solely upon Allah

Thus taken together, this means that the Messiah will lead his community to higher, God-centered moral ground. The Messiah will protect the true believers through spiritual strength, not by material means. Furthermore, this hadith most clearly signifies that no one will have the power to make an outward contest with Gog and Magog. This is something that the Muslims believe in – a fairy tale that the Messiah and Mahdi will wage war against Gog and Magog. However, as we can see, this is not what the Hadith implies.

The Promised Messiah will then be instructed through revelation to take refuge at mount Tur with his Jama’ah, i.e. worship and prayers will be brought to attention, and it is through prayer and heavenly signs that the Jama’ah of the Promised Messiah will ideologically conquer these powerful nations and spread its message.

Hadith Explained by Khalifatul Masih IV (RH)

Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad (RH), 4th Caliph of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community explains this eloquently below:

“The Holy Prophet, referring to the latter days, prophesied Gog and Magog will rule the world and they will rise wave after wave and the whole world will be overwhelmed by the waves of their power. At that time the Messiah will be raised in the world and the Messiah with his followers will try to fight them, and will attempt to counter them. Allah will then speak to the Messiah saying: that no man in the world has been granted the power to fight these two nations which We have created – not even you! There is only one way, that you seek shelter on a mountain and pray to God. It is only the weapon of prayer that can subjugate these nations.”
[The Gulf Crisis and New World Order, Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad, pp.68-69]

What does the Mountain Represent?

Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad (RH) explains in the very next section of the book, titled “The Jamaat of the Muhammadan Messiah and Its Responsibilities,” that the mountain mentioned in the prophecy should not be understood solely as a physical mountain. Rather, it represents the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) and the lofty teachings, character, and example that he brought.

A summary of his explanation is presented below in bullet points:

• The Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) is the spiritual mountain to which the believers are instructed to seek refuge. Just as a mountain provides protection and strength, believers find spiritual strength by returning to the teachings and example of the Holy Prophet (SAW).

• The prophecy therefore instructs the believers to take refuge in the teachings of Islam and then turn to Allah through prayer. Prayers offered while following the lofty principles of the Holy Prophet (SAW) will receive Divine support.

• This responsibility falls particularly upon the Jama’at of the Promised Messiah (AS). The prophecy indicates that, when worldly powers fail and people lose faith in prayer, the Messiah’s Community will remind the world that prayer is the true means of seeking Allah’s help.

• The purpose is not simply to protect Ahmadis from worldly difficulties, but to revive the spiritual strength of the Muslim Ummah by bringing people back to Allah and the example of the Holy Prophet (SAW).

• Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad (RH) emphasizes that Ahmadis should continue praying persistently, particularly during periods of worldwide turmoil, because there is ultimately no lasting solution to the world’s spiritual and moral problems without turning to Allah.

• The condition for this Divine help is that the Community must seek refuge in the spiritual eminence of the Holy Prophet (SAW) and strive to follow his teachings, character, and noble example.

Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS): Prayers are the only solution against Gog and Magog

In his commentary on specific verses of the Holy Quran, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS), the Promised Messiah and Mahdi, expands on several verses of Surah Al-Anbiyaa which pertain to the coming of Gog and Magog and state of latter days. He expounds on this verse below:

حَتّٰۤی اِذَا فُتِحَتۡ یَاۡجُوۡجُ وَمَاۡجُوۡجُ وَہُمۡ مِّنۡ کُلِّ حَدَبٍ یَّنۡسِلُوۡنَ ﴿۹۷﴾

“It shall be so even when Gog and Magog are let loose and they shall hasten forth from every height.”
[Quran 21:97]

Ahmad (AS) explains in his commentary that the latter days will be the time when Ad-Dajjal and Gog and Magog will be rampant on Earth and will be responsible for various immoralities and sins present on the Earth. He explains that the coming of the Messiah is assosciated with Ad-Dajjal and Gog and Magog. However, Ahmad (AS) clearly states that based on Quran and Ahadith, the Messiah will use the power of prayer only to defeat the enemies of God.

کیونکہ یا جوج ماجوج کی تعریف حدیثوں میں یہ بیان کی گئی ہے کہ ان کے ساتھ لڑائی میں کسی کو طاقت مقابلہ نہیں ہوگی اور مسیح موعود بھی صرف دعا سے کام لے گا
“[…] Because the definition of Gog and Magog as described the Ahadith is that no one will be able to compete with them in a fight and that the Promised Messiah will only utilize [the power/weapon of] prayer.“

[Tafseer Masih Maud, Volume 5, p. 355]

Following the Messiah’s Teaching: The Khulafa and the Weapon of Prayer

Just as the Promised Messiah (AS) emphasized that prayer is the only means through which believers can overcome Gog and Magog, all the Khulafa-e-Ahmadiyyat have followed his teachings and repeatedly urged the Jama’at to pray fervently and sharpen their weapon of prayer. Prayer is the only weapon possessed by the heavenly Jama’at of Allah, and it is through this weapon that Divine help and protection are sought.

Although the Khulafa have emphasized the importance of prayer repeatedly in their lectures, sermons, and books, one excerpt from each Khalifa will be presented below to highlight this emphasis.

Khalifatul Masih I (RA)

When Hazrat Hakim Maulwi Nooruddin (RA) was seriously ill in 1911, one of his final messages to the Jama’at was to sharpen the weapon of prayer, as others had abandoned it:

“[…] That is the weapon of prayer which the whole world has abandoned. Among Muslims, our community should intensify this work and make use of it. As far as possible for them, they should offer prayers and not grow weary. I am so ill that it cannot even be conceived how much of my life is left; therefore, this is my final testament/will to the Jama’at: along with La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah), sharpen the weapon of prayer.”

[Haqaiq-al-Furqan, Surah Al-Mu’minun, p.105] [Al-Badr, Volume 10, Number 10, dated January 12, 1911, page 3]

Khalifatul Masih II (RA)

During his 52 years of Khilafat, no Khalifa was as emphatic in urging the Jama’at to pray as the Promised Son (RA). He repeatedly reminded the Jama’at that prayer is the only means of success and urged them to pray as it is the only means that the Jama’at of the Messiah will successfully defeat Satanic forces of the modern world. He gave several lectures on this – one of his lectures is linked below.

تمہارے پاس صرف دعا کا ہتھیار ہے۔ سو تم اپنے لیے،
سلسلہ کے لیے اور تمام بنی نوع انسان کے لیے خوب دعا ئیں کرو

Lecture Title: “You only have the weapon of prayer, so pray for yourself, for your loved ones, and for all of humanity.”

[Khutbat-e-Mahmood, Vol. 32, p.104]

Khalifatul Masih III (RH)

Hazrat Mirza Nasir Ahmad (RH) that only through the weapon of prayer can Ahmadis pull the world from evils to the fountain of life:

“[…] But as I said, we do not have external supplies/resources; we have only one thing, the only weapon that has been given to us, and that weapon is mighty. The world cannot compete with it, and that is the weapon of prayer. So this is the weapon that was given to us, and its quality and nature were explained to us, and a certainty in prayer was granted to us, and God has said that although the task is difficult, it must happen. Because humanity at this time is passing through a delicate/critical period, and this task is entrusted to you, but I will not give you supplies, yes, I give you the weapon of prayer. So through prayer, draw/pull the world to the fountain of life […]”

[Khutbat-e-Nasir, Vol 1, p.1020]

Khalifatul Masih IV (RH)

The view of Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad (RH) is presented above.

Khalifatul Masih V (ABA)

Like all the previous Khulafa, Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad (ATBA) has repeatedly emphasized that the Promised Messiah’s (AS) victory over satanic forces depends upon prayer. An excerpt is presented below:

“May Allah grant us the ability to fulfill this mission which the Promised Messiah, peace and blessings be upon him, brought —which is to bring the world under the banner of the Holy Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. For this purpose, utilize all your capabilities and efforts, and pray to the utmost limit, because the dominance of the Promised Messiah, peace be upon him, is destined to happen through prayers. You have been given the weapon of prayer […]”
[Khutbat-e-Masroor, Volume 15, p. 315-316 (Friday Sermon delivered on June 30, 2017)]

Furthermore, in the Friday Sermon of August 23, 2024, Hazrat Khalifatul Masih V (ABA, based on a previous vision of Khalifatul Masih III|
(RH), instructed the Jama’at to recite certain prayers everyday explaining that through these prayers, believers will be safeguarded in a
secure fortress against Satan.

Special Appeal for Prayers:

His Holiness (aba) said that he wished to make an appeal; the Third Caliph (rh) saw a vision in which an elder said to him that every adult in the Community should recite Durood Sharif [prayer for invoking salutations upon the Holy Prophet (sa)] SubhanAllahi wa bi Hamdihi SubhanAllahil Azeem Allahumma Salle ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad (Holy is Allah and worthy of all praise, Holy is Allah the Great, O Allah bestow Thy blessings upon Muhammad and the people of Muhammad) 200 times. Those who are 15-25 years of age recite it at least 100 times, and if children recite it at least 33 times and parents help their infant children recite it at least three to four times. Then recite Astaghfiruallha Rabbi Min Kulli Zanbinwwa Atubu Ilaih (I seek forgiveness from Allah, my Lord, for all my sins and turn to Him) 100 times. His Holiness (aba) said that he would also include the prayer Rabbi Kullu Shay’in Khadimuka Rabbi Fahfazni Wansurni Warhamni (My Lord everything is subservient to You; My Lord protect me, help me and have mercy on me) to be recited not just in these days but generally as well.

According to the vision of the Third Caliph (rh), the elder said that if these were recited then you will become safeguarded in a secure fortress, impenetrable by Satan, made with iron walls reaching the heavens.

His Holiness (aba) said that these days when Satan is trying to attack our Community and the world at large, the only way for us to remain safeguarded is through prayers. Hence, we should recite these prayers, not just during the days of Jalsa but throughout the year.

Conclusion

• Gog and Magog cannot be defeated through worldly power; the Holy Prophet (sa) taught that the Messiah’s refuge would be in Allah and prayer.

• The Promised Messiah (as) identified prayer as the weapon through which his Community would overcome these powerful forces.

• His Khulafa have continued to emphasize this same teaching, repeatedly reminding the Jama’at that our strength and success depend upon sincere, fervent prayer.

Introduction

Non-Muslims often raise erroneous allegations on Prophet Muhammad (SAW) and Khulafa-e-Rashideen. Below is a beautiful refutation of one such allegation by Hazrat Maulwi Nooruddin (RA). The original accusation was made by Pundit Lekh Ram, an Arya Samaj leader and one of the staunchest opponents of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Jama’ah.

Narration from biography of Khalifatul Masih I (RA)

Khalifatul Masih Awwal, Hakim Maulwi Nooruddin (RA) states:

“Once, the governor of that place, Pandit Radhakrishan Sahib, said to me at Raja Amar Singh’s place: ‘Some of the objections raised by Lekh Ram against Islam are totally unanswerable. Muslims cannot respond to them.’

I said: ‘The matter is very easy. Present before me, at this moment, the strongest of those objections, and Raja Sahib will be our judge.’

Thereupon, he raised this objection regarding the library of Alexandria that it was burnt on the order of Hadhrat Umar (RA).

I asked him: ‘In your opinion, is there any authentic book of history in the world, in which any historian, between the Islamic first, second, third, or fourth century, has stated this story?’

He said: ‘I have not read the Arabic books on history.’

I said: “You know I have not read the English histories. But alright, now name any English history that is relatively reliable.“

Then he mentioned ‘The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire by Gibbon.’

I said: “This one book will be decisive between you and me, let it be brought.”

Consequently, that book was brought from Dewan Amarnath Sahib’s library, and whatever that author had opined about the library, was presented before Governor Sahib.

[After reading the excerpt from the history book] He gave such an astonishing reply:

‘Since we are taught right from the beginning that the religion of Islam is very bad, any objection raised against it seems tremendously glorious to us.’

[Mirqatul Yaqeen fi Hayat-e-Nuruddin p. 174-175]

Excerpt from the Book: ‘The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire’

“For my own part, I am strongly tempted to deny both the fact and the consequences. The fact is indeed marvellous; “Read and wonder!” says the historian himself: and the solitary report of a stranger who wrote at the end of six hundred years on the confines of Medina, is overbalanced by the silence of two annalists of a more early date, both Christians, both natives of Egypt, and the most ancient of whom, the patriarch Eutychius, has amply described the conquest of Alexandria. The rigid sentence of Omar is repugnant to the sound and orthodox precept of the Maho-metan casuists: they expressly declare, that the religious books of the Jews and Christians, which are acquired by the right of war, should never be committed to the flames; and that the works of profane science, historians or poets, physlelans or philosophers, may be ‘lawfully applied to the use of the faithful. […]”

[The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire by Edward Gibbon, Vol. III, p.213]

Conclusion

In the 19th century, relentless campaigns against Muslims severely distorted the public perception of Islam. Emulating his spiritual master, the Promised Messiah (AS)—who was actively penning books to defend Islam from Christian and Hindu attacks—Hazrat Maulwi Nooruddin (RA) also always remained ever-ready to counter and refute these allegations.
