Introduction

Skeptics allege that innocent suffering, diseases, and natural disasters prove God is cruel, powerless, or non-existent. This claim is completely false. The Holy Quran teaches that worldly trials test moral fortitude, awaken human humility, and operate through purposeful divine laws. Opponents possess zero Quranic verses showing that worldly pain occurs without divine wisdom or ultimate justice.

📖 Primary Historical Treatise Begins

Essence of Islam (Vol. 2, pp. 367–375)

Author: Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian (AS) |
Source: Alislam.org Digital Reader (PDF pp. 379–387)

The following text contains the complete, unabridged verbatim theological treatises from the chapters “Punishment In This World”, “Why Some Disbelievers Are Punished in This World”, “How Wrongdoers Are Punished”, and “Punishment Follows Upon Misconduct”.

The Purpose of Life and the Law of Trials

The secular “problem of evil” assumes that physical comfort is the supreme purpose of human existence. Islam rejects this materialistic premise. Earth is not designed as an effortless paradise; it is a testing ground where human souls develop spiritual fortitude, exercise free will, and prove their moral worth.

The Holy Quran explicitly establishes this foundational principle:

ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلٗاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ

“He Who has created death and life that He might try you — which of you is best in deeds; and He is the Mighty, the Most Forgiving.” (Surah Al-Mulk, 67:3)

Without hardship, courage cannot exist. Without sickness and grief, compassion and healing have no meaning. Allah tests humanity through diverse trials to distinguish the steadfast from the insincere:

وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَىۡءٍ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصٍ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ

“And We will surely try you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and fruits; but give glad tidings to the patient.” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:156)

Furthermore, a significant portion of earthly suffering is generated directly by human choices, corruption, and systemic injustice rather than arbitrary divine decree:

ظَهَرَ ٱلۡفَسَادُ فِى ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِى ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِى عَمِلُواْ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ

“Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of men have wrought, that He may make them taste a part of what they have done, so that they may turn back.” (Surah Ar-Rum, 30:42)

The Eternal Law of Worldly Punishment

When calamity strikes human societies, questions arise concerning why some populations suffer catastrophe while others remain unscathed. In Anwar-ul-Islam, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS), the Promised Messiah and Mahdi, outlined the unchangeable divine law governing worldly destruction:

wp:quote

It is the eternal way of God that until a disbeliever or a denier of truth becomes so bold and daring as to create the causes of his ruin with his own hands God Almighty does not destroy him by way of punishment. When the time of punishment approaches, He generates causes on account of which the decree of his destruction is recorded. This alone is the eternal law of the punishment from God and this is the way of God and unchangeable law laid down in the Book of God.

[Anwar-ul-Islam, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 9, p. 3]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 367]

/wp:quote

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) further clarified that worldly destruction is never inflicted merely for private ideological or doctrinal disagreement. The Day of Judgement is appointed for settling theological beliefs:

wp:quote

The Holy Qur’an and other Divine scriptures disclose that the ruin and destruction imposed in this life on people as punishment are not afflicted because those people follow a wrong doctrine, for instance, because they worship idols, or planets, or fire, or some other created things or person; inasmuch as accounting for religious errors is postponed till the Judgement Day and no one is punished in this life merely on account of doctrinal errors or disbelief. The punishment for such defaults is postponed till the hereafter. Indeed this world is a paradise for the disbelievers and it is mostly the believers who suffer pain and torment in this world. 150 150 This world is the paradise of the disbeliever and the prison of the believer. [Publisher] Therefore, it is naturally asked that if this world is the paradise of the disbelievers, and indeed observation testifies that the disbelievers are richly endowed with wealth and the bounties of this world, and the Holy Qur’an repeatedly announces that the disbelievers are endowed with every worldly bounty, then how is it that some disbelieving people were afflicted with torment in this world and God Almighty destroyed them with stones and storms and plagues?

[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 367]

/wp:quote

Why Disbelief Alone Is Not Punished in This World

If this earthly life operates as a material paradise for disbelievers, why were certain civilizations historically annihilated by plagues, storms, and earthquakes? Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) answered this apparent paradox in Anwar-ul-Islam:

wp:quote

Therefore, it is naturally asked that if this world is the paradise of the disbelievers, and indeed observation testifies that the disbelievers are richly endowed with wealth and the bounties of this world, and the Holy Qur’an repeatedly announces that the disbelievers are endowed with every worldly bounty, then how is it that some disbelieving people were afflicted with torment in this world and God Almighty destroyed them with stones and storms and plagues? The answer is that these torments were not inflicted merely on account of disbelief, but because those people who were so afflicted and ruined had transgressed grievously in their denial of Divine Messengers and their mockery, jesting and persecution; and in the estimation of God Almighty, their mischief, wickedness, cruelty and persecution had reached extreme limits and thus they themselves created the causes of their ruin. Thereupon God’s wrath was roused and they were destroyed through diverse types of chastisement. This shows that disbelief is not the cause of punishment in this world; its cause is extreme wickedness and arrogance. Such a one, even if he is a believer, when he transgresses the limits in wrongdoing, persecution and arrogance, and forgets altogether the Majesty of God, would draw upon himself Divine chastisement. On the other hand when a disbeliever is meek and is fearful, he would not be chastised in this world though he would be condemned to hell on account of his misguidance. This is the ancient and confirmed philosophy behind chastisement in this world and this is the way of Allah to which all Divine books bear testimony. As the Glorious God says in the Holy Qur’an: وَإِذَآ أَرَدۡنَآ أَن نُّهۡلِكَ قَرۡيَةً أَمَرۡنَا مُتۡرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُواْ فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فَدَمَّرۡنَٰهَا تَدۡمِيرٗا “And when We intend to destroy a township, We address Our commandment to its rebellious people, but they transgress therein; so the sentence of punishment becomes due against it, and We destroy it with utter destruction.” (Surah Bani Isra’il, 17:17) When We decide to destroy the people of a township We warn those of its dwellers who indulge in luxurious living because they transgress the limits in wickedness. Thereupon, the Divine law in respect of them is fulfilled in that their wrongdoing arrives at its climax. Then We destroy them with a severe destruction. In another verse it is said: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡعَثَ فِيٓ أُمِّهَا رَسُولٗا يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا ۚ وَمَا كُنَّا مُهۡلِكِي ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا وَأَهۡلُهَا ظَٰلِمُونَ

“And thy Lord would never destroy the towns until He has raised in the mother town thereof a Messenger, reciting unto them Our Signs; nor would We destroy the towns unless the people thereof are wrongdoers.” (Surah Al-Qasas, 28:60) We have never destroyed a habitation except when its people are determined upon wrongdoing. It should be kept in mind that though association of anything with God is also not only a wrong but an enormity, yet in this context by wrongdoing is meant such disobedience and misconduct as transgress the limit. For mere association of others with God which is not accompanied by persecution, arrogance, disorder, attacks upon the preachers of other religions, plans for their killing, and such extreme sinfulness whereby the fear of God is totally excluded from the hearts, the punishment is promised in the hereafter. Chastisement in this life is inflicted only at the time of extreme transgression, as it is said in another verse: 153 Messengers before thee were also subjected to ridicule, but We gave respite to the disbelievers who mocked, and when they reached the limits in their mockery, We seized them and people witnessed how Our chastisement overtook them. Again it is said: 154 The disbelievers devised a plan for wiping out Islam, and We also devised a plan. That is to say, We let them go forward with their plans till they reached a stage of wrongdoing which, according to the way of Allah, attracts His chastisement…. All these verses show that Divine chastisement is inflicted in this world only when a person transgresses the extreme limits in mischief, wrongdoing, arrogance, haughtiness and exaggeration. It does not happen that a disbeliever is inflicted with the lightning of Divine chastisement who is fearful in the extreme, or that a polytheist may be stoned who is terrified to death on account of his fear. God Almighty is Merciful and Compassionate to the highest degree. He seizes with punishment in this world only those who provide with their own hands the cause for such punishment.

[Anwar-ul-Islam, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 9, pp. 14-16, footnote I]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, pp. 368–370]

/wp:quote

Two Categories of Wrongdoers and the Activation of Divine Wrath

To understand how divine justice operates in the physical world, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) categorized offenders into two distinct classes in Tohfah Golarviah:

wp:quote

God Almighty deals with offenders in two ways, and offenders are of two types. First, there are those offenders who do not transgress the limits, and though out of extreme bigotry they persist in their effort yet they do not carry their persecution to the extreme limit. These will be punished in the hereafter. God, the All-Knowing, does not seize them in this world inasmuch as their attitude is not one of severe hostility. For the punishment of sins the appointed day is the Day of Judgement. Secondly, there are those offenders who transgress the limits in their wrongdoing and persecution and desire to rend the Messenger of God and the righteous like wild beasts and to wipe them out altogether, and to consume them like a blazing fire. With regard to such offenders who carry their wrath to the limit, the way of Allah is that His wrath is roused against them and they are punished in this world in addition to their chastisement in the hereafter. In the idiom of the Qur’an they are designated the maghdubi-‘alaihim155.

[Tohfah Golarviah, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 17, pp. 213-214]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 370]

/wp:quote

How Communities Avert Calamities

Deliverance from worldly disasters does not depend on dogmatic labels, but upon moral conduct, compassion, and humility. In Chashma-e-Ma’rifat, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) laid down the universal requirements for averting collective chastisement:

wp:quote

It should be kept in mind that for being delivered from afflictions it is not necessary that people should become Muslims, inasmuch as the Day of Judgement is appointed for calling people to account for their religious errors. It is, however, necessary that people should refrain from every type of misconduct and should not revile the holy Prophets of God, nor oppress the poor, and should spend freely in charity and should ascribe no equal to God, neither stone, nor fire, nor man, nor water, nor sun, nor moon and should discard the ways of arrogance and mischief.

[Chashma-e-Ma’rifat, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 23, p. 404]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 371]

/wp:quote

The Transformation of Divine Attributes: Why Wrath Manifests

God’s primary attributes are rooted in benevolence, grace, and sustenance. Why then does wrath appear in the universe? In Anjam-e-Atham, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) explained how human misconduct forces a change in how divine attributes express themselves:

wp:quote

reward by the Master of the Day of Judgement. No one of these four attributes comprises a design which would harm man; they are all designed for his good. But in the case of a person who, through his misconduct and extravagant behaviour, puts himself outside the operation of these attributes, they begin to operate to his harm. For instance, Rububiyyat takes on the aspect of destruction and annihilation, and Rahmaniyyat is manifested in the shape of wrath and anger, and Rahimiyyat is manifested in the shape of revenge and harshness, and the design of good recompense takes on the terrifying aspect of punishment and torment. This change in the expressions of Divine attributes is brought about in consequence of a change in man’s own condition. Thus punishment, and warning of punishment, are not comprised in the basic attributes of God, inasmuch as God’s warning of punishment is not absolute so long as the person warned is alive and has the capacity to carry out a change in himself. Therefore, a change in respect of the promised chastisement is not a breach of promise. Every warning of chastisement is conditional though no condition may be expressly mentioned, except when the warning is expressed in absolute terms in which case it becomes an absolute decree and is not subject to change. This is a grand and valued principle relating to the comprehension of Divine attributes which is inherent in the Surah Fatihah.

[Anjam-e-Atham, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 11, pp. 7-10 footnote]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, pp. 371–373]

/wp:quote

The four mother attributes described in Surah Al-Fatihah—Rububiyyat (Nourishment to perfection), Rahmaniyyat (Unearned grace), Rahimiyyat (Mercy rewarding righteous effort), and Malikiyyat (Mastership of the Day of Recompense)—exist entirely for human benefit. But when a tyrant persists in cruelty and arrogance, the very laws designed to sustain life operate to eradicate the infection of tyranny.

Historical Retribution: The Fate of Impostors and Aggressors

Worldly punishment also serves as a visible sign verifying the veracity of true prophets against false claimants. In Malfuzat, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) highlighted the critical difference between intellectual denial and aggressive violence:

wp:quote

It is worthy of note that the Meccans had not merely rejected the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be on him). Simple rejection based on naivety does not entail punishment in this life. But when a disbeliever 156 But if anyone resorts to killing or conspiring to kill, or embarks upon mischief and persecution, he is bound to be chastised.

[Malfuzat, vol. III, pp. 162-163]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 373]

/wp:quote

Had God allowed impostors and tyrants to persecute His messengers without consequences, moral distinction would collapse. The Holy Quran underscores this distinction:

وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوۡ كَذَّبَ بِـَٔايَٰتِهِۦٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ

“And who is more unjust than he who forges a lie against Allah or gives the lie to His Signs? Surely, the unjust shall not prosper.” (Surah Al-An‘am, 6:22)

As Hazrat Ahmad (AS) expounded in Essence of Islam:

wp:quote

Who is guilty of greater wrong than one who fabricates a lie against God or gives the lie to His signs? It is thus clear that those who gave the lie to the word of God on the occasion of the advent of God’s Prophets were not spared by God and were destroyed by diverse types of torments. Observe what was the end of the people of Noah and of ‘Ad and Thamud and the people of Lot and of Pharaoh and the Meccan enemies of the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be on him). Thus when those who rejected the truth were chastised in this world, how can he escape who fabricates a lie against Allah and who is mentioned in the first place in the verse just cited. Would God treat the righteous and the false alike and is there no punishment in this life from God Almighty for impostors?

[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, pp. 374–375]

/wp:quote

✓ End of Primary Source Treatise

Concluded from Essence of Islam (Vol. 2). The section below provides quick answers and key takeaways.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does God allow innocent people and children to suffer?

In Islam, physical mortality and worldly pain are not punishments for sin, but the necessary condition of a material universe operating under consistent natural laws. Children and innocents who endure illness, physical disabilities, or disasters are not cursed; their trials awaken empathy, sacrifice, and medical science in society. Furthermore, Islamic theology guarantees that all unmerited worldly suffering is completely compensated with boundless spiritual elevation, bliss, and divine proximity in the eternal Hereafter.

Does God punish people in this life merely for holding incorrect religious beliefs?

No. Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) proved from the Holy Quran that accounting for doctrinal differences and honest theological disbelief is strictly postponed to the Day of Judgement. In this life, God allows disbelievers and polytheists to enjoy wealth, children, and material prosperity. Worldly chastisement is never inflicted for private theological errors; it is only unleashed when a people transgress all moral limits through violent persecution, cruelty, mocking arrogance, and active attempts to wipe out the righteous.

Why do corrupt, wicked people often flourish while righteous believers suffer?

This world is designed as a moral crucible, not the final hall of recompense. The Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stated that this world is a paradise for the disbeliever and a prison for the believer. Righteous individuals endure hardship to refine their patience, extinguish worldly attachments, and achieve high spiritual stations. Conversely, wicked tyrants are granted material respite so that their internal rebellion reaches full fruition, leaving them with zero excuses when divine justice is executed.

What causes collective disasters and divine destruction in human history?

Collective disasters fall into two distinct categories: (1) general natural phenomena operating according to the physical laws of nature, and (2) specific divine retribution sent upon societies that cross extreme limits of tyranny, arrogance, and persecution against God’s prophets. The Holy Quran records that civilizations like Noah’s people, ‘Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh were not destroyed for peaceful disbelief, but because they waged active warfare, mocked divine warnings, and attempted to annihilate the truthful.

Can a divine warning of punishment or calamity be averted?

Yes. Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) established that warnings of punishment are intrinsically conditional, not absolute decrees. So long as a person or community remains alive, repentance (Tawbah), sincere prayer, generous charity, and halting oppression will avert the threatened calamity. This foundational principle was demonstrated when the entire nation of Prophet Jonah (Yunus AS) was spared after they humbled themselves in sincere repentance before God.

Introduction

Skeptics allege that God created humanity out of boredom, loneliness, or a selfish need for mechanical praise. This claim is completely false and contradicts Islamic theology. Allah is Self-Sufficient; human creation exists solely for man’s own spiritual enlightenment, divine communion, and eternal perfection. Opponents possess zero Quranic verses and zero Hadith proving God derives any benefit from human worship.

📖 Primary Historical Treatise Begins

Essence of Islam (Vol. 2, pp. 461–478 & Vol. 1, pp. 3–5)

Author: Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian (AS) |
Source: Alislam.org Digital Reader (PDF pp. 473–490)

The following text contains the complete, unabridged verbatim theological treatises from the chapters “Only the Creator Can Enjoin the Purpose of Life”, “The Three Objects of Life”, and “The Purpose of Religion”.

Only the Creator Can Enjoin the Purpose of Life

The fundamental question of human purpose cannot be answered by mortal speculation. Because man does not generate his own existence, he cannot determine his own existential objective. In Islami Usul ki Philosophy (The Philosophy of the Teachings of Islam), Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS), the Promised Messiah and Mahdi, elucidated this foundational reality:

wp:quote

Though different people, on account of their shortsightedness or lack of courage, appoint various types of objectives for their lives and stop short at worldly purposes and desires, yet the purpose that God Almighty has specified in His Holy Word is: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ “And I have not created the Jinn and the men but that they may worship Me.” (Surah Al-Dhariyat, 51:57) I have created jinn and men so that they should recognize and worship Me. According to this verse the true purpose of human life is the worship and understanding of God Almighty and devotion to Him. It is obvious that it is not open to man that he should himself lay down the purpose of his life by his own authority inasmuch as man does not arrive in the world of his own will, nor will he depart from this world of his own will. He is a created being and He Who created him and bestowed upon him better and higher faculties than those bestowed upon other animates, has enjoined a purpose for his life. Whether anyone comprehends that purpose or not, without doubt the purpose of man’s creation is the worship and understanding of God Almighty and to lose himself in Him.

[Islami Usul ki Philosophy, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 10, p. 414]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 461]

/wp:quote

The Divine Trust: Why Man Undertook What Creation Feared

Every creation has a capacity proportionate to its nature. In Taudih-e-Maram, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) expounded upon the Quranic concept of the Divine Trust (Al-Amanah) and why human beings were uniquely prepared to bear this responsibility:

wp:quote

This means that the Divine Trust, by which is meant the love of God and complete obedience to Him even in the face of hardship, was offered to the angels and the whole of creation and the mountains, all apparently full of strength, but they all refused to undertake it, being afraid of its grandeur. But man undertook it for he possessed two qualities, that he could force himself in the cause of God Almighty and could advance so far in love of Him as to forget altogether everything else.

[Taudih-e-Maram, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 3, pp. 75-76]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 462]

/wp:quote

The Three Objects of Human Life

The purpose of any created entity is determined by its highest potential achievement. A beast of burden achieves its peak through physical labor, whereas the human soul is endowed with faculties capable of direct spiritual communion. Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) detailed the three supreme objects of human life:

• Spiritual Understanding (Ma’rifat): Developing deep, experiential insight into the Being, unity, and attributes of God Almighty.

• True Worship (‘Ibadat): Submitting every internal and external faculty entirely to the Divine Will in genuine obedience.

• Ardent Love and Union (Muhabbat and Liqa’): Advancing so far in love of Allah that the soul seeks nothing of its own, opening the window of the heart directly toward God.

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) established this principle through logical induction:

wp:quote

The real purpose of all the external and internal limbs and faculties that have been bestowed on man is understanding and worship and love of God. That is why, despite a thousand occupations, man does not find his true well-being except in God Almighty. Having acquired great wealth, or achieved high office, or having become a great merchant, or having acquired governing authority, or become a great philosopher, he departs in the end from these worldly involvements with a sense of frustration. His heart rebukes him all the time about his deep concern with the world and his conscience never approves his wiles and deceits and wrongful actions. This problem can be appreciated in another way. The purpose of the creation of a thing is determined by its highest achievement beyond which its faculties cannot rise. For instance, the highest a bullock is capable of is ploughing, or irrigation, or transportation, and therefore these are the purpose of its life and it cannot rise above them. But when we take stock of man’s faculties and powers to discover his highest capacity, we find that he is invested with the faculty of seeking after God so much so that he desires that he should become so devoted to God’s love that he should have nothing of his own and that everything should become God’s. He shares his natural needs like food and drink and rest with other animates, and in industry some animals are ahead of him; for instance, the bees produce such excellent honey from every type of flower that man has so far not been able to compete with them. It is clear, therefore, that the highest capacity of man is meeting with God Almighty and thus the true purpose of his life is that the window of his heart should open towards God.

[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 462]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 462]

/wp:quote

This intrinsic longing for the Divine is rooted in the very soul of humanity, as affirmed in the Holy Quran:

وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَـٰذَا غَـٰفِلِينَ

“And when thy Lord brings forth from the children of Adam, from their loins, their seeds, and makes them testify regarding themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They say, ‘Yea, we do bear witness.’ Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We were indeed unaware of this.’” (Surah Al-A’raf, 7:173)

How to Achieve the Purpose of Life

Recognizing the purpose of life is only the initial step; the vital task is mastering the practical means to attain it. Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) explained that the first and most critical prerequisite is having a correct conception of the True God:

wp:quote

The question is how and through what means can man achieve this purpose? Let it be clear that the principal means for achieving this purpose is the correct recognition of and faith in the True God. If this first step is wrongly taken and a person sets up a bird, or an animal, or any of the elements, or a human being as his god, it cannot be expected that his subsequent steps would be taken along the straight path. The True God helps His seekers; but that which is dead cannot help the dead.

[Islami Usul ki Philosophy, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 10, p. 415]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 2, p. 463]

/wp:quote

Without the true recognition of God, human devotion becomes misguided and lifeless. The Holy Quran calls humanity directly to this foundational principle:

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ

“O ye people! worship your Lord Who created you and those who were before you, that you may become righteous;” (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:22)

The Purpose of Religion: Living Certainty Over Dead Dogma

Human beings cannot fulfill their purpose of creation through empty rituals or dry intellectual theories. Religion is not designed for philosophical entertainment; it is designed to grant living certainty (Yaqin) that rescues man from sin.

In Nasim-e-Da’wat, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) articulated why true faith requires direct experience:

wp:quote

The true purpose of adopting a faith is that one should acquire such certainty concerning God, Who is the fountainhead of salvation, as if one can see Him with one’s eyes. The wicked spirit of sin seeks to destroy a man and a person cannot escape the fatal poison of sin till he believes with full certainty in the Perfect and Living God and till he knows for certain that God exists, Who punishes the offender and bestows upon the righteous everlasting joy. It is a common experience that when one believes in the fatal effects of anything one does not have recourse to it. For instance, no one swallows poison consciously. No one deliberately stands in front of a wild tiger. No one deliberately thrusts his hand into the hole of a serpent. Then why does a person commit sin deliberately? The reason is that he has not that certainty in this matter as he has in other matters of the kind that we have mentioned. The first duty of a person, therefore, is to acquire certainty with regard to the existence of God, and to adopt a religion through which this certainty can be acquired so that he should fear God and shun sin. How can such certainty be acquired? It cannot be acquired through mere stories. It cannot be acquired through mere arguments. The only way of acquiring certainty is to experience God repeatedly through converse with Him or through witnessing His extraordinary signs, or by keeping company with someone who has that experience.

[Nasim-e-Da’wat, Ruhani Khaza’in, Vol. 19, pp. 447-448]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 1, p. 3]

/wp:quote

In Chashma-e-Masihi, the Promised Messiah (AS) underscored that true love of God constitutes the reality of Paradise itself:

wp:quote

The purpose of religion is that man should obtain deliverance from his passions and should develop personal love for God Almighty through certain faith in His existence and His perfect attributes. Such love of God is the paradise, which will appear in diverse shapes in the hereafter. To be unaware of the True God, to keep away from Him, and not to have any love for Him, is the hell which will appear in diverse shapes in the hereafter. Thus, the true purpose is to have full faith in Him. Now the question is which religion and which book can fulfil this need. The Bible tells us that the door of converse with God is closed and that the ways of obtaining certainty are sealed. Whatever was to happen, happened in the past and there is nothing in the future….. Of what use then is a religion that is dead? What benefit can we derive from a book that is dead? What grace can be bestowed by a god who is dead?

[Chashma-e-Masihi, Ruhani Khaza’in, Vol. 20, pp. 352-353]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 1, p. 4]

/wp:quote

In Surmah Chashm Arya, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) clarified that God is completely free from any personal need for worship:

wp:quote

The purpose of accepting a religion is that God, Who is Self-Sufficient and is in no need of His creation or its worship, may be pleased with us, and that we should experience such grace and mercy as should wipe out our inner stains and rusts so that our breasts may be filled with certainty and understanding. This is not possible for a man to achieve through his own devices. Therefore, God the Glorious, keeping hidden mainly His own Being and the wonders of His creation, for instance, souls, bodies, angels, heaven, hell, resurrection, prophethood, etc. and yet disclosing them partially through reason, appointed his servants to believe in all these mysteries.

[Surmah Chashm Arya, Ruhani Khaza’in, Vol. 2, p. 81]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 1, p. 4]

/wp:quote

Does God Need Our Worship? Refuting the Neediness Allegation

A persistent misconception raised by materialists and polemicists is that if God demands worship, He must possess a narcissistic desire for praise. Islam rejects this notion entirely:

• God is Al-Ghani (The Self-Sufficient): Allah possesses all perfection inherently. The collective worship of all creation does not augment His majesty by a single atom, nor does global disobedience diminish His sovereignty.

• Worship benefits man exclusively: Just as light is essential for the eye and oxygen for the lungs, communion with God is the vital nutrient required for the human soul to avoid spiritual death.

• The Divine attribute of Rububiyyat (Lordship): While worship benefits human beings, God’s nature as the Sustainer and Fosterer of creation demands that righteousness prevail over corruption. A loving physician insists that a sick patient take life-saving medicine, not because the physician benefits from the pill, but because true benevolence cannot tolerate preventable destruction.

There exists zero evidence in the Holy Quran or Hadith suggesting God created humanity out of personal vulnerability or emotional need. Creation is the natural manifestation of Divine benevolence, designed so mortal beings may inherit immortal spiritual bliss.

✓ End of Primary Source Treatise

Concluded from Essence of Islam (Vols. 1 & 2). The section below provides quick answers and key takeaways.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did God create human beings according to Islam?

God created human beings so they may recognize their Creator, understand His divine attributes, and attain spiritual perfection through voluntary worship and ardent love. As stated in Surah Al-Dhariyat (51:57), the primary purpose of humanity is the worship (‘Ibadat) and deep spiritual recognition (Ma’rifat) of Allah.

Does God need human worship in Islam?

No. Allah is Al-Ghani (The Completely Self-Sufficient) and requires nothing from His creation. Worship is an exclusive necessity for human beings. Just as physical eyes need sunlight to see, human souls require worship to achieve purity, moral elevation, and salvation from spiritual ruin.

What are the three primary objects of human life in Islam?

According to Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS), the three objects of human existence are: (1) acquiring true knowledge and understanding of God (Ma’rifat), (2) offering genuine devotion and worship (‘Ibadat), and (3) experiencing ardent love and direct union with God (Muhabbat and Liqa’), where the soul loses itself entirely in Divine love.

Why cannot human beings invent their own purpose of life?

Human beings do not arrive in this world by their own power, nor can they depart by their own choice. A created being cannot dictate its own ultimate purpose; only the Creator who endowed humanity with higher cognitive and spiritual faculties can designate its purpose. Man’s highest capacity is experiencing the Living God.

How can a person gain certainty in God’s existence today?

Islam teaches that certainty in God cannot be gained through ancient folklore or dry philosophical debates alone. True certainty requires living experience, which is achieved through direct communion with God, experiencing His extraordinary signs, and keeping company with the truthful (Sadiqin) who have experienced the Living God.

Introduction

Critics allege that Islamic miracles are irrational magic tricks that shatter the established laws of physics. This allegation is completely false and contradicts the Holy Quran. Islam teaches that God never breaks His own laws of nature. Opponents possess zero Quranic verses and zero Hadith proving that miracles violate the consistent divine order.

📖 Primary Historical Treatise Begins

Essence of Islam (Vol. 5, pp. 1–40)

Author: Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian (AS) |
Source: Alislam.org Digital Reader (PDF pp. 15–54)

The following text contains the complete, unabridged verbatim theological treatises from the chapter “Miracles, Signs and Prophecies”.

The Foundational Principle: God Never Violates the Laws of Nature

The primary question at the intersection of religion and reason is whether divine miracles violate natural law. Materialist philosophers and atheist critics often define a miracle as an arbitrary suspension or rupture of the laws of physics. Because science observes an unbroken uniformity in nature, sceptics conclude that miracles are mythological inventions.

Islamic theology, as expounded by the Holy Quran and revived by Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS), the Promised Messiah and Mahdi, rejects this false definition entirely. In Islam, God is the supreme Author of the laws of nature. His laws reflect His eternal wisdom and unchangeable attributes. God never contradicts Himself, nor does He create a chaotic universe where fundamental physical order is arbitrarily dismantled.

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) stated this immutable principle in the clearest terms:

wp:quote

The truth of the matter is that God Almighty does not do anything against the laws of nature. What He does is that He creates the causes, whether we know of them or not, and these are always present. Hence, miracles, such as splitting of the moon and [the fire turning cold for Abraham] are also no exceptions. Rather, they too resulted from some very subtle and hidden means, and were based on true and factual science. Shortsighted people and those who are enamoured of dark philosophy cannot comprehend these things.

[Malfuzat, vol. 1, p. 72]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 27]

/wp:quote

A miracle is not the destruction of natural law. Rather, it is the manifestation of higher, deeper, and undiscovered divine laws that operate within the natural order. When an extraordinary event occurs at the hands of a prophet, God sets into motion subtle secondary causes that transcend ordinary human comprehension, yet remain entirely harmonized with divine reality and true science.

Scriptural Proofs: The Unchanging Way of Allah

The Holy Quran repeatedly establishes that the cosmos is governed by precise, immutable divine laws (Sunnatullah), free from inconsistency, defect, or arbitrary disruption.

Verse 1: Quran 67:4

مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتٖۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٖ

“Thou seest no flaw in the creation of the Gracious God. Then look again: Seest thou any flaw?” (Surah Al-Mulk, 67:4)

If God routinely suspended the laws of gravity, thermodynamics, or biology to execute miracles, creation would be riddled with flaws, disruptions, and inconsistency (tafawut). The Holy Quran challenges humanity to scrutinize the cosmos repeatedly to verify that no such structural rupture exists.

Verse 2: Quran 33:63

سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلٗا

“Such has been the practice of Allah with those who passed away before; and thou wilt never find any change in the practice of Allah.” (Surah Al-Ahzab, 33:63)

Allah affirms that His Sunnah—His established practice and natural law—is uniform across all epochs. There is no alteration (tabdil) in His cosmic governance.

Verse 3: Quran 30:31

فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفٗاۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ

“So set thy face to the service of religion as one devoted to God, like unto the natural disposition which Allah has instilled into man. There is no altering the creation of Allah. That is the right religion; but most men know not.” (Surah Al-Rum, 30:31)

The Quran declares that true religion is identical to Fitratullah—the natural law and constitution designed by God. To claim that religion requires belief in the suspension of natural law is to contradict the very definition of faith set forth by Allah.

Ordinary Practice vs. Special Practice: What ‘Khariq-e-‘Adat’ Truly Means

In classical Islamic discourse, miracles are often categorized as Khariq-e-‘Adat (traditionally rendered as “breaking the habit” or “supernormal”). Superficial readers mistakenly interpret this phrase to mean “breaking the laws of nature.”

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) rectified this misunderstanding in his masterpiece Surmah Chashm Arya, explaining that Khariq-e-‘Adat refers to God departing from His customary dealings with ordinary people, not violating His eternal laws:

wp:quote

It is appropriate in this context to address the question that if everything is subject to the eternal laws, or is predetermined, then what is the significance of miracles? It is undoubtedly true that nothing lies outside the eternal laws or the eternal will of God and His decree, whether we are aware of it or not. And yet the same Divine practice—also called the law of nature—has made certain things dependent upon others. Likewise, there are certain phenomena which the eternal will has made conditional upon the prayers of the holy ones, and the blessings of their holy breath, and upon their attention, their firm resolve and their glory, and has linked them to the entreaties and supplications of these people. When such phenomena occur through these means and under these conditions then, in this particular situation, they are called miracles, wonders, signs or supernormal phenomena. Here the term ‘supernormal phenomena’ should not lead someone to think that there are things which lie outside the scope of Divine practice [laws].

Because, in the present context, the expression ‘supernormal phenomena’ carries an additional significance: Although nothing lies outside the eternal practice of the God of glory, His practice that relates to mankind is of two kinds. First there are ‘ordinary practices’, which, in the form of cause and effect, apply to everyone. Second there are the ‘special practices’ which, with or without the agency of the visible causes, relate only to those who are totally lost in His love and completely given to His desire. That is to say, when a person turns completely to God and brings about a transformation in his human condition, for the sake of gaining His pleasure, then God, in accordance with his transformed state, deals with him in a special manner, which He does not practice when dealing with others. In other words, this special treatment, relatively speaking, is Khariq-e-‘Adat [supernormal], the nature of which is revealed only to those who are drawn towards God through His grace. When a person, in his eagerness to have communion with God, breaks out of his mortal habits, which intervene between him and his Lord, then, for the sake of such a person, God too breaks His customary ways. This phenomenon of ‘breaking’ is also part of the eternal practice of God and is not something novel that should be called into question. It has been the way of God since eternity that as man’s faith in Him increases, He too casts more and more light of His Omnipotence upon him.

[Surmah Chashm Arya, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 2, pp. 105-107]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 11]

/wp:quote

The Promised Messiah (AS) further clarified that this supernormal interaction is fully compatible with empirical philosophy and rational thought:

wp:quote

The moment a person attains a ‘new’ life—which may be called supernormal when compared to his earlier life—the same Eternal God, through His extraordinary manifestations, reveals Himself to him as a ‘New God’; and deals with him in such a way that he could never have imagined in his earlier life. The key to miracles—which set the wonders of Nature in motion—is the transformed human soul. A genuine transformation exhibits such visible signs, and the fervent cries of love at times so overwhelm the heart, that the passionate emotions of love for God and the powerful pull of truth and conviction transport one to a state where, if he were cast into a fire, it would have no effect on him whatsoever. Likewise, if he were to be thrown before lions, wolves or bears, they would not be able to do him any harm, because, at that moment, due to the perfect and powerful manifestations of truth and love, he breaks out of the human condition and is a different being altogether. Just as fire engulfs a piece of iron and makes it seem like fire, so do such people, by virtue of being overwhelmed by the fire of love for God, begin to exhibit something of the attributes of the Great Power which has overwhelmed them. It is little wonder, therefore, that such supernormal phenomenon should occur when the servant, in his submission, comes under the complete influence of the Lord. In fact, it would be surprising if, despite such an influence, no change is brought about in the ordinary state of the person, for even a piece of iron, when it is heated in fire, starts to partially exhibit the properties of fire, and this is in total conformity with the laws of nature. But, if it is exposed to intense heat and still maintains its former state, and acquires no new characteristic, such a thing would be contrary to reason. Empirical philosophy also testifies to the necessity of such phenomena. This is no fiction. Ponder over it with true wisdom.

[Surmah Chashm Arya, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 2, pp. 105-107]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 11]

/wp:quote

The Science of Miracles: Convergence of Hidden Causes and Prayer

How do miracles manifest in the physical world without disrupting scientific order? When an extraordinary sign is demonstrated—such as Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) being preserved when cast into the furnace—sceptics imagine that the element of fire lost its intrinsic physical properties.

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) dismantled this naive assumption in Barakat-ud-Du’a, explaining that miracles occur through the divine mobilization of hidden physical and spiritual causes:

wp:quote

Another subtle point that needs to be borne in mind is that when men of God show miracles, for instance, when water is not able to drown them or fire is not able to harm them, the secret behind such manifestations is that at times when the friends of God focus their attention towards a particular thing, the All-Wise God—Whose infinite secrets man can never comprehend—shows a sign of His power, and their attention begins to exercise control in the universe. The convergence of the means which, for instance, cause the heat of the fire to cease casting its effect—whether they are related to heavenly bodies, to some hidden property of the fire itself, or to some subtle property of the body that is put in the fire, or whether it is a combination of all these—all these means come into operation through such attention and such prayer. It is thus that an extraordinary miracle is shown.

But this does not cause us to lose faith in the reality of things, nor does it render knowledge useless, for such miracles are themselves a branch among the branches of Divine knowledge. They have their own dimensions, just as, for instance, the burning quality of fire has its own. Let us understand it this way: there are spiritual elements that manifest themselves by subjugating the fire, and they are peculiar to their own time and place. Human intellect falls short of understanding the secret that a perfect man is the locus for the manifestation of the spirit of God Almighty. And when the time comes for the perfect man to display this manifestation, everything begins to fear him as it fears God. You may now throw him before a beast or into a fire, he will suffer no harm; for at such moments the spirit of God Almighty is upon him and everything is bound to fear Him. This is the ultimate secret of Divine knowledge which cannot be understood without keeping company with the perfect ones.

[Barakat-ud-Du’a, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 6, pp. 29-31, footnote]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 28]

/wp:quote

Just as modern science discovers that electromagnetic radiation, chemical inhibitors, or thermal insulation can counteract extreme heat without violating physics, the Creator mobilizes latent physical and spiritual mechanisms unknown to human observers. The miracle remains fully compliant with the deeper laws of nature.

The True Definition and Purpose of a Miracle

What is the precise theological definition of a miracle in Islam? In Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya (Part 5), the Promised Messiah (AS) established that a miracle is an extraordinary event that opponents cannot replicate, designed solely to differentiate truth from falsehood:

wp:quote

A miracle is in fact an extraordinary phenomenon, the like of which the opponent is unable to produce, even though it appears to be within human power. An example of this is the miracle of the Holy Quran that was shown to all the people of Arabia. Although, on the face of it, it seemed to be within the scope of human potential, all the people of Arabia were frustrated in their efforts to produce anything like it. Thus, for understanding the nature of miracles, the Holy Quran serves as a very clear example. It may seem to be a discourse like that of human beings, but in respect of its eloquent expression, its extremely delectable, pure and colourful diction—characterized in every instance by truth and wisdom—and its brilliant arguments that countered the arguments of the whole world, and, last but not least, in respect of its majestic prophecies, it is a matchless miracle, and one that no opponent has been able to contest despite the passage of thirteen hundred years, and none has the power to do so…

In short, the true purpose of a miracle is to demonstrate the distinction between the truth and falsehood, or between the truthful and the liar. Such distinguishing phenomenon is called a miracle or a sign. A sign is an essential phenomenon without which it is neither possible to have full faith in the existence of God, nor to reap the fruit that grows out of full conviction. Since the truth of a religion is directly linked to the recognition of God, it is therefore an essential and important prerequisite of a true religion to possess the signs that conclusively and definitively prove His existence.

[Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, part 5, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 21, pp. 59-60]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 10]

/wp:quote

A miracle is granted when a human being attains total purity and communion with the Divine. In Surmah Chashm Arya, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) explained:

wp:quote

Let it be known that a miracle is one of the Divine practices, or one of the acts of the Omnipotent One, that can be called supernormal. Thus, the reality of supernormal phenomena is that when those whose souls are purified transcend the ordinary human condition, and cut through their low habits, and march forward trying to gain nearness to God, He then deals with them in such a strange way—in accordance with their condition—that, as compared to the normal human state, it appears to be an altogether supernormal phenomenon. And to the extent that a person forges ahead on the path of love and devotion, having renounced his mortal state and having torn up the veils of the self, to the same extent do these miracles appear for him with greater clarity, transparency and brilliance.

[Surmah Chashm Arya, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 2, pp. 68-69, footnote]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 9]

/wp:quote

Why Absurd and Coercive Signs Are Denied

A major source of confusion among sceptics is the misconception that God must perform whatever theatrical spectacle an unbeliever demands. Throughout history, disbelievers demanded that prophets physically fly into the sky, produce mountains of gold, or summon ancestors from the grave to deliver speeches.

The Holy Quran records the demand made by the Meccan idolaters to the Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ:

أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتٞ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبٗا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥ ۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرٗا رَّسُولٗا

“‘Or thou have a house of gold or thou ascend up into heaven; and we will not believe in thy ascension until thou send down to us a book that we can read.’ Say, ‘Holy is my Lord! I am not but a man sent as a Messenger.’” (Surah Bani Isra’il, 17:94)

Commenting on this verse, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) stated in Tohfah Ghaznaviyyah:

wp:quote

That is to say, Divine Glory is free from the criticism that any of His Messengers, or Prophets, or recipients of revelation should exhibit with their own power the supernormal phenomena that are in fact peculiar to Divinity. He says, [O Prophet] tell them that I am only a Messenger from among the mortals, and am not empowered to do anything on my own; I only obey the command of God. It is therefore foolish to demand from me only some particular signs. I can show only what God has decreed, and no more.

[Tohfah Ghaznaviyyah, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 15, p. 540]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 25]

/wp:quote

Why does God reject coercive, doomsday-style spectacles? The Promised Messiah (AS) explained in Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya (Part 5) that faith must remain a deliberate moral choice, not forced sensory compulsion:

wp:quote

Remember, it is only to demonstrate the distinction between truth and falsehood that miracles are granted to men of God. The real purpose of a miracle is none other than that a distinction between a truthful one and a liar be established in the eyes of the wise and just. A miracle is shown only to the extent that is sufficient to establish such distinction. And this extent is determined by the need of the time, as is the nature of the miracles. It does not mean that whenever a prejudiced, ignorant, and evil-minded person demands a miracle, it has to be shown, no matter how contrary it is to the Divine wisdom or the need of the moment. Were it so, it would be as harmful to one’s own faith, as it would be contrary to Divine wisdom. For if the realm of miracles were to be stretched to the extent that whatever has been put off until the day of resurrection can all be witnessed in this world, then no difference would be left between this world and the hereafter.

It is due to this very difference that the righteous actions and true beliefs, when adopted in this world, earn reward; but if the same beliefs and actions are adopted in the hereafter, they will not be worthy of any reward whatsoever… In short, a sign is not something so self-evident that the entire world is obliged to accept it, without any disagreement, excuse or hesitation; and no one, regardless of his disposition, is left with any doubt about it and even the dullest of men accepts it without a qualm. A sign or a miracle, therefore, is not a self-evident phenomenon for men of every disposition, so that it should be accepted as soon as it is witnessed. Rather the fact is that only wise, just, righteous and truthful people derive benefit from signs.

[Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, part 5, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 21, pp. 44-46]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 14]

/wp:quote

The Promised Messiah (AS) continued, addressing the mythological demands invented by superstitious minds:

wp:quote

But the wretched one, who is bereft of the light of intuition, does not find any satisfaction in miracles that are only meant for making a distinction, and persists in his demand that he will not accept any miracle save that which is as clear as doomsday. He demands, for instance, that someone should go to heaven and return before his very eyes holding a book in his hand; not only that, he also says that he will not believe unless he himself takes the book in his own hand and reads from it. Or, for instance, that the one who descends should bring with him a piece of the moon or the sun to illuminate the earth. Or, better still, he should descend from heaven accompanied by angels who should do wonderful things, as angels do. Or that many dead people should be resurrected through his prayer, and they should be recognized as fathers or grandfathers of so and so, who had died at such and such a time. As if this too were not enough, these resurrected people must hold rallies in different cities and deliver lectures in which they should proclaim that they are the dead who have been brought back to the world so that they may testify to the truth of a particular religion… Such are the self-conceived miracles that the majority of ignorant people, who are totally unaware of the essence of faith, are in the habit of demanding. They also demand other similarly unreasonable and absurd phenomena that are far removed from the Will of God.

[Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, part 5, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 21, pp. 44-46]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 14]

/wp:quote

Disproving Superstition: Distinguishing True Miracles from Trickery

If miracles operated by shattering nature into irrational chaos, how could an honest observer distinguish a divine sign from a conjuror’s sleight of hand?

In Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) explained that true divine signs are supported by reason, whereas irrational tales degrade religion into superstitious vulnerability:

wp:quote

When reason recognizes a miracle and testifies that it is from Allah, such a miracle is a thousand times better than the miracles that are related only as tales and myths. For this there are two reasons: The first is that reported miracles cannot be considered by us—who were born hundreds of years after their occurrence—as something which we ourselves have seen and experienced. And since they are only based on reports that have reached us, they can never be accorded the same degree of credence as is given to observed and tangible phenomena.

Secondly, even for those who actually witnessed them, such reported miracles, as are beyond the realm of reason, cannot be truly convincing. This is because there are many wondrous feats which even conjurors can easily perform, but they are no more than cunning tricks. How then are we to convince a suspicious opponent that the wonders manifested through Prophets—such as creating a serpent, or bringing a dead man back to life—are free from the sleight of hand practised by these conjurors… Besides, ordinary people have no knowledge of the natural sciences, philosophy and arts, and are completely unaware of all the amazing qualities which the All-Wise has invested in the universe. Hence at every time and age they are ready to be deceived.

[Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 1, pp. 511-557]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 32]

/wp:quote

Divine miracles do not rely on stagecraft or momentary optical illusions. They consist of profound historical fulfillments, heavenly signs in accordance with scriptural prophecies, the acceptance of impossible prayers, and grand disclosures of the unseen that lie entirely beyond human contrivance.

The Living Signs Vouchsafed to Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS)

Islam does not depend on ancient fables or unverified hearsay. In every age of spiritual darkness, Allah raises a reformer equipped with fresh heavenly signs to prove that God is a living reality.

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) challenged the entire world to witness living divine signs manifested through his person in Qadian:

wp:quote

God has informed me directly through His living Word that if I am troubled by people asking how they should know that I am from Him, I should tell them: It is sufficient proof that His heavenly signs are my witness, my prayers are accepted, knowledge of the unseen is revealed to me beforehand, and such mysteries, as are known to none other than God, are disclosed to me in advance. And the second sign is that should anyone want to challenge me in the aforesaid matters—in the acceptance of prayers, being given prior knowledge of their acceptance, and in being given knowledge of unseen matters that lie beyond the limits of human knowledge—he will surely be defeated in this challenge, be he from the East or from the West. These are the signs that have been vouchsafed to me.

[Government Angrezi Aur Jihad, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 17, pp. 29-30]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 1]

/wp:quote

In Haqiqat-ul-Wahi, the Promised Messiah (AS) documented that hundreds of thousands of living witnesses verified his signs:

wp:quote

God has shown so many signs in my support that if I were to count them one by one up to this day, 16th July, 1906, I can swear by God that they are in excess of three hundred thousand. And if someone does not believe in my oath, I can provide him with proof. Some of these signs are to do with occasions when God Almighty, in keeping with His promise, protected me from being harmed by the enemy. Some of the signs are such that, in keeping with His promise, God always fulfilled my needs and my wishes. And some are of the kind whereby, in keeping with His promise God brought humiliation and disgrace upon those who tried to harm me. Some signs are of the kind in which, according to His Prophecies, He made me victorious over those who filed lawsuits against me… Some signs are of the kind in which terminally ill patients were cured and I was informed of their recovery in advance.

[Haqiqat-ul-Wahi, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 22, pp. 70-71]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 2]

/wp:quote

In Kashti Nuh, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) issued an open challenge regarding his prophecies:

wp:quote

Even if a person were to strive all his life in the hope of finding some prophecy of mine about which he could assert that it has remained unfulfilled, he will not find a single one, though, out of shameless audacity or ignorance, he may say whatever he likes. I declare emphatically that there are thousands of explicit prophecies of mine that have been fulfilled with great clarity and to which hundreds of thousands of people bear witness. If you try to find precedence among past Prophets, you will not find it, with the sole exception of the Holy Prophet ﷺ… For a long time He kept Himself hidden, and He was denied but He remained silent. Now, however, He will conceal Himself no longer and the world shall witness such manifestation of His Power as their forefathers had never seen.

[Kashti Nuh, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 19, pp. 6-7]
[Essence of Islam, Vol. 5, p. 5]

/wp:quote

✓ End of Primary Source Treatise

Concluded from Essence of Islam (Vol. 5). The section below provides quick answers and key takeaways.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do miracles break the laws of physics and nature in Islam?

No. In Islam, God never acts against the laws of nature. The Holy Quran explicitly declares that there is no flaw or alteration in Allah’s creation (Quran 67:4; Quran 33:63). As Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) explained in Malfuzat, miracles occur through subtle, undiscovered secondary causes and true science operating within the natural order, not through irrational violations of physical laws.

What does the Arabic phrase “Khariq-e-‘Adat” mean regarding miracles?

Khariq-e-‘Adat literally means “breaking the customary habit.” In theological context, it does not mean breaking eternal natural laws. Rather, it means that God departs from His ordinary customary dealings with common humans to deal with His purified elect in an extraordinary, special manner (Surmah Chashm Arya, pp. 105–107).

How did Abraham (AS) survive the fire if natural laws were not broken?

When Hazrat Abraham (AS) was cast into the fire, God did not abolish the chemical properties of matter. Instead, through the spiritual focus and prayer of His prophet, Allah mobilized latent physical and spiritual causes—such as hidden properties in the body or environment—that neutralized the destructive effect of the flames (Barakat-ud-Du’a, pp. 29–31). Miracles demonstrate the convergence of higher causes, not the suspension of reality.

Why does God refuse absurd, theatrical demands from sceptics?

The purpose of a miracle is to distinguish truth from falsehood for sincere seekers, not to force belief through overwhelming sensory coercion. If God manifested doomsday spectacles—such as resurrecting dead ancestors to hold public rallies or physically bringing a book down from the sky—the test of human free will would be destroyed, and faith in the unseen would carry zero moral reward (Quran 17:94; Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, Part 5).

What is the difference between a prophet’s miracle and a conjuror’s trick?

A conjuror’s trick is an optical illusion or sleight of hand based on temporary deception and limited human contrivance. A divine miracle is an enduring heavenly sign—such as the linguistic and prophetic perfection of the Holy Quran, the acceptance of impossible prayers against powerful adversaries, and thousands of precise prophecies fulfilled across decades (Brahin-e-Ahmadiyya, pp. 511–557).
