Introduction

The prophecy of Muhammadi Begum is one of the most powerful signs proving the truthfulness of Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS). When arrogant relatives stomped on the Holy Quran and challenged God to show a sign in their family, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) warned that Mirza Ahmad Baig would die within three years of marrying his daughter, Muhammadi Begum, to someone else. Ahmad Baig openly defied the warning and married Muhammadi Begum away on April 7, 1892—and in just 5 months and 23 days, God struck him dead right on time! Even his fiercest opponents admitted the death of Ahmad Baig fulfilled the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum, the surviving husband testified to the miracle, and the entire family repented and entered Islam Ahmadiyyat.

Why Did God Target This Family?

This was never a private family argument over a marriage proposal.

The people involved in this incident were first cousins and close in-laws of Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) living in Qadian and Hoshiarpur:
1. Mirza Nizam-ud-Din and Mirza Imam-ud-Din: First cousins of Hazrat Ahmad (AS).
2. Mirza Ahmad Baig: Their brother-in-law, who lived in Hoshiarpur.
3. Muhammadi Begum: The eldest daughter of Mirza Ahmad Baig.

These relatives did not just leave religion quietly. They turned into hardcore atheists who completely abandoned Islam, hurled insults at Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and attacked religion.

Look at what they were actually doing:
1. Denying the existence of God: They claimed that God does not exist and that all religions are just tricks played by smart men.
2. Stomping on the Holy Quran: They literally placed physical copies of the Holy Quran under their feet and stomped on them in front of others.
3. Worshipping an idol: Mirza Imam-ud-Din abandoned Islam entirely and became the leader of the Lal Begi community. He published pamphlets claiming a sweeper deity named Balmik was his savior and called the God of Muslims an idol [Deed-e-Haq, p. 5; Gul-e-Shaguft, p. 12].
4. Blocking Muslims from praying: Mirza Nizam-ud-Din and Imam-ud-Din even built a brick wall across the public street to block Muslims from going to the Mubarak Mosque to pray behind Hazrat Ahmad (AS). The British court later forced them to knock it down [Siraj-e-Munir, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 12, pp. 69–70].

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) wrote about their terrible state:

إِنَّ اللّٰهَ رَأَىٰ أَبْنَاءَ عَمِّي، وَغَيْرَهُمْ مِنْ شُعُوْبِ أَبِيْ وَأُمِّيْ الْمَغْمُوْرِيْنَ فِي الْمُهْلِكَاتِ… وَالْمُنْكِرِيْنَ لِوُجُوْدِ اللّٰهِ وَمِنَ الْمُفْسِدِيْنَ

“God Almighty saw my paternal cousins and other close relatives that they are indulged in soul-crushing activities… denying the existence of Allah, and creating mischief.”

[A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, pp. 566–567]

He also mentions an eyewitness who ran to his house in tears:

“One night, a man came to me weeping. I asked him in fear: ‘Have you heard news of someone’s death?’ He replied: ‘No, something far worse! I was sitting with those relatives who have turned apostate from God’s religion. One of them hurled such vile abuse at the Holy Prophet ﷺ as I have never heard from any disbeliever. Furthermore, I saw them place the Holy Quran beneath their feet and stomp on it. They were uttering words that make the tongue tremble, saying that God does not exist and is merely a myth concocted by fabricators.’ Upon hearing this, my heart shattered, tears flowed from my eyes, and I locked my door and fell in prostration before God, begging for His intervention.”

[A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, pp. 568–570]

The Relatives Demanded a Sign First

Did Hazrat Ahmad (AS) pick this family out of nowhere?

Not at all. The relatives themselves demanded a heavenly sign inside their own household.

In August 1885, Mirza Ahmad Baig, Mirza Nizam-ud-Din, and Mirza Imam-ud-Din wrote an aggressive public letter. They published it in the newspaper Chashma-e-Nur. They even joined hands with Pandit Lekh Ram, the infamous Hindu Arya Samajist who spent his life attacking Islam. Mirza Imam-ud-Din signed this challenge on August 13, 1885, and Pandit Lekh Ram published it directly in his anti-Islam book Takzib Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya (Kulliyat Arya Musafir, p. 415).

Primary source scan: The public tract signed by Mirza Imam-ud-Din on August 13, 1885, published in Pandit Lekh Ram’s anti-Islam book Takzib Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya (Kulliyat Arya Musafir, p. 415), proving the relatives joined hands with Hindu opponents to demand a heavenly sign against Hazrat Ahmad (AS).

Their demand was very simple:
– They mocked all the logical arguments and proofs of Islam published in Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya.
– They demanded that God show a direct sign of life and death inside their own immediate family.
– They publicly declared that unless God showed a sign in their household, they would never believe in Islam.

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) turned to Allah in prayer:

“O my Lord! Help Your servant and disgrace Your enemies.”

[A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, p. 568]

God answered his prayer in August 1885 with a clear promise:

إِنِّيْ رَأَيْتُ عِصْيَانَهُمْ وَطُغْيَانَهُمْ فَسَوْفَ أَضْرِبُهُمْ بِأَنْوَاعِ الْآفَاتِ أُبِيْدُهُمْ مِنْ تَحْتِ السَّمَاوَاتِ… وَلٰكِنْ لَّا أُهْلِكُهُمْ دَفْعَةً وَّاحِدَةً بَلْ قَلِيْلًا قَلِيْلًا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُوْنَ وَيَكُوْنُوْنَ مِنَ التَّوَّابِيْنَ

“I have observed their disobedience and transgression. I shall soon strike them with various calamities and destroy them from under the heavens… Yet I shall not destroy them all at once, but step by step, so that they may turn back and be among those who repent.“

[A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, pp. 569–570]

Notice this crucial point right from day one. God clearly said the punishment would not wipe them out in a single second. It would strike step by step, specifically to give them a chance to turn back and repent!

The 31-Month Countdown Sign (August 5, 1885)

In that exact same month of August 1885, God answered their challenge with an astonishingly specific countdown prophecy:

“I received a revelation regarding Imam-ud-Din and Nizam-ud-Din that within a period of thirty-one months, a severe calamity would strike them; that someone from their family would die, leaving them in intense shock and trauma. This will happen from today’s date, which is August 5, 1885.”

[Tadhkirah, p. 103]

Did anything happen within 31 months?

Exactly in the thirty-first month (March 1888), Mirza Nizam-ud-Din’s young daughter suddenly died, leaving behind a newborn baby!

In 1886, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) had also seen a vision warning their mother:

“Repent, repent! Or calamity shall befall your daughter or your granddaughter.”

[Tadhkirah, revelation of 1886, pp. 107–108]

Notice this: at this point, Muhammadi Begum was not even in the picture yet. God was already showing this household pinpoint signs of life and death down to the exact month, warning them to repent before the proposal was ever made.

How the Prophecy of Muhammadi Begum Started

In 1888, Mirza Ahmad Baig found himself in trouble.

His sister’s husband had gone missing years earlier and was presumed dead. Ahmad Baig wanted to transfer that ancestral property into his own name, but British land law required the written consent of other family heirs. That meant he desperately needed Hazrat Ahmad (AS) to sign legal consent papers.

Ahmad Baig came to Hazrat Ahmad (AS) and begged him for his signature.

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) told him that he does not take such steps without praying to Allah for guidance. When he prayed, God revealed the entire matter:

“The All-Powerful and Glorious God revealed to me: ‘Propose to Ahmad Baig that he give his eldest daughter, Muhammadi Begum, in marriage to you. Tell him that if he accepts, it will bring immense blessings and mercy upon him. But if he refuses, and marries her to someone else, the girl’s father will die within three years of that marriage, and the man who marries her will die within two and a half years of the wedding, and calamities will overtake their household, unless they repent and turn to God.'”

[Announcement of July 10, 1888; A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, p. 572]

Think about how wise this divine plan was.

If Ahmad Baig agreed, family ties would be healed, their attacks on Islam would end, and the cousins would return to faith peacefully.

But if Ahmad Baig arrogantly refused and continued his war against Islam, God’s warning would fall upon him.

Why Was the Prophecy Kept Private at First?

Christian missionaries later objected in their newspaper Nur Afshan: “If this revelation was truly from God, why did Mirza Sahib keep it private at first and ask the family not to publish it?”

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) gave a very simple and honorable answer:

It was a private family matter. He did not want to cause heartbreak, public shame, or pain to Ahmad Baig and his daughter. He wanted to give them a peaceful chance to reconcile.

So who made it public?

It was the girl’s own maternal uncle, Mirza Nizam-ud-Din! In a fit of fury, Nizam-ud-Din took the private letter, ran through the bazaars, shouted the details to everyone in town, and handed it over to the hostile Christian missionary newspaper Nur Afshan!

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) wrote:

“The response is that this was a private affair and it had been communicated to those for whom it was meant to be a Sign. It was also certain that the publication would offend the father of that girl. Therefore, I desisted because of the possibility of such heartache and pain… Mirza Nizam-ud-Din, the maternal uncle of the girl, in a fit of rage and fury, himself published it and published it so widely that perhaps within one or two weeks, ten thousand men and women were informed… He had my letter published in the newspapers and paraded it throughout the bazaars… Now that this letter of mine has been published even in Nur Afshan, and the Christians have begun to utter falsehoods regarding it, it is my duty to reveal the facts with my own pen.”

[A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, pp. 287–288 / Mirror of Excellences of Islam, p. 328]

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) then pointed out a crushing fact that completely destroys the cheap attack of “marriage desire”:

Years earlier, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) had already told Pandit Lekh Ram and the entire clan that a man from their family named Ahmad Baig was destined to die!

At the time that initial death prophecy was made, Muhammadi Begum was only 8 or 9 years old!

As Hazrat Ahmad (AS) explained: How could a warning about her father’s death be driven by “lust” or personal desire when the prophecy of his death was already made when his daughter was just a little child?

Calamities Strike Before Muhammadi Begum’s Wedding

Anti-Ahmadis completely skip the four years between 1888 and 1892.

Why? Because if they told you what happened, their whole objection would fall apart.

Even before Ahmad Baig married Muhammadi Begum to someone else, God began fulfilling the promise made in 1885 that calamities would strike them “step by step”:
1. His young son died: Ahmad Baig’s beloved young son died suddenly.
2. His first sister died: Ahmad Baig’s sister (the wife of Ghulam Hussain) died unexpectedly.
3. His second sister died: Another sister passed away shortly after.
4. Heavy financial losses: The family faced severe financial setbacks.

Ahmad Baig saw his own son and sisters dying one after another. Yet, his arrogance blinded him. Instead of taking heed and repenting, he decided to openly defy God’s warning.

On April 7, 1892, Mirza Ahmad Baig married his daughter Muhammadi Begum to a relative named Mirza Sultan Muhammad of Patti.

The clock had now officially started.

Did Ahmad Baig Die on Time After Muhammadi Begum’s Wedding?

The divine prophecy gave Ahmad Baig up to three years from the date of Muhammadi Begum’s wedding to die.

Did he survive three years?

Did he survive two years?

Did he even survive one year?

Not at all. Mirza Ahmad Baig did not even make it to six months!

In late September 1892, Ahmad Baig suddenly fell ill with a severe typhoid fever. His condition collapsed in a matter of hours. He was rushed to the municipal hospital in Hoshiarpur, but nothing could save him.

Within just 48 hours of falling sick, Ahmad Baig died!

He passed away on September 30, 1892.

That was just 5 months and 23 days after Muhammadi Begum’s wedding!

The man who mocked Islam, demanded a heavenly sign, stomped on the Quran, and laughed at God’s warnings was dead and buried in under six months.

This was a massive, terrifying fulfillment of prophecy witnessed by thousands of people across India.

Even Opponents Conceded the Muhammadi Begum Prophecy Was Fulfilled

Did the opponents back in 1892 say the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum had failed?

Not even close! They were completely stunned.

Maulvi Muhammad Hussain Batalwi was the number one enemy of Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS). He spent his whole life issuing fatwas against him. Yet, when Ahmad Baig dropped dead, even Batalwi had to openly admit in his own magazine that the prophecy was fulfilled right on time!

Because he could not deny the death, Batalwi came up with an absurd excuse:

مرزا صاحب کی پیشگوئی کے مطابق احمد بیگ کا میعاد کے اندر مر جانا علم نجوم یا رمل یا جفر کے ذریعے سے ہو سکتا ہے

“The death of Ahmad Baig within the appointed time in accordance with Mirza Sahib’s prophecy could have been calculated through astrology, geomancy, or jafar [divination].”

[Isha’at-us-Sunnah, Vol. 15, pp. 22–23]

Just look at how desperate the opponents were!

An orthodox Muslim scholar was forced to claim that a fulfilled prophecy was “astrology and fortune-telling.”

If the prophecy had failed, Batalwi would have celebrated in the streets. Instead, he had to invent excuses to explain why Ahmad Baig died on time!

Why Didn’t Muhammadi Begum’s Husband Die?

Now comes the favorite question of modern anti-Ahmadis:

“If the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum was true, why didn’t her husband, Mirza Sultan Muhammad, die within two and a half years?”

The answer is very simple: because God spared him when the family repented.

In Islam, all warnings of punishment have a condition: if people fear God and repent, God holds back the punishment.

When Ahmad Baig dropped dead in under 48 hours, the entire family went into absolute shock.

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) describes what happened immediately after Ahmad Baig’s death:

“There were two parts to this prophecy. One related to Ahmad Baig and the other to his son-in-law. And some revelations published earlier contained the condition that in case of repentance (taubah) and fear, the death would be delayed. However, Ahmad Baig ridiculed the prophecy until his time arrived, and he passed away from this world in a day or two from typhoid fever. Only then did their eyes open and they became terrified for the son-in-law as well. Their women became gripped with fear of God, weeping, offering Salat, fasting, and trembling in terror. Thus, at such a time of intense fear, it was impossible that God’s established law would not show mercy.”

[Siraj-e-Munir, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 12, p. 32]

What about the husband himself?

Mirza Sultan Muhammad did not act like Ahmad Baig. He did not mock Hazrat Ahmad (AS). He did not insult Islam. Instead, he became deeply fearful, wrote respectful letters, and sought forgiveness.

Because they turned to God with tears and repentance, God fulfilled His eternal promise:

وَمَا كَانَ اللّٰهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوْنَ

“And Allah would not punish them while they were seeking forgiveness.”

[Surah Al-Anfal, 8:34]

God Revealed That Only One Man Would Die

Right from the beginning, God made it clear that both men would not die.

In July 1888, Allah revealed to Hazrat Ahmad (AS):

يَمُوْتُ وَيَبْقٰى مِنْهُ كِلَابٌ مُّتَعَدِّدَةٌ

“One man shall die, and multiple dogs shall remain behind barking.”

[Announcement of July 15, 1888; Tadhkirah, p. 108]

Look at the Arabic word يَمُوْتُ (yamutu). In Arabic, this word means one single man will die. If God meant that both Ahmad Baig and the husband were going to die, the Arabic word would be يَمُوْتَانِ (yamutani—two men will die).

God revealed from day one that only one man was destined to die! Ahmad Baig died, and the husband repented and was saved.

The Simple Example of Poisoned Food

In his book Haqiqat-ul-Wahi (pp. 224–225), Hazrat Ahmad (AS) gave a very simple example to explain this:

Imagine two men sit down to eat from a plate of food. They are warned beforehand that the food is poisoned.

The first man laughs, ignores the warning, eats the food, and drops dead.

The second man watches him die in horror. He drops his fork, starts shaking, breaks down in tears, and begs for help.

Would any fair person force the second man to eat the poison and die too?

Of course not!

Ahmad Baig was the first man. He laughed and died within six months. When he died, the husband saw what happened, dropped his arrogance, and turned to God in fear. God does not destroy someone who repents!

Look at Prophet Jonah (Yunus AS)

Anti-Ahmadis want you to believe that if a punishment does not strike, the prophet was false.

If that logic is true, what will they say about Prophet Jonah (Yunus AS)?

Prophet Yunus (AS) gave an unconditional warning to his entire city:

“Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”

[Book of Jonah, 3:4]

Did Nineveh get destroyed on day 40?

No! Not a single person died.

Why? Because the entire city put on sackcloth, wept, and repented before God. The Holy Quran explicitly confirms this:

فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيْمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُوْنُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوْا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا

“Why was there no other people, save the people of Jonah, who should have believed so that their belief would have profited them? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the present life.”

[Surah Yunus, 10:99]

Now ask any anti-Ahmadi:
– Did Prophet Yunus (AS) become a false prophet because Nineveh was spared?
– Of course not! Every Muslim respects him as a true prophet of God.

Why the double standard against the Promised Messiah (AS)?

When Ahmad Baig died, the family repented, and God showed mercy to the husband. That is the exact same way Allah dealt with the people of Prophet Yunus (AS).

Muhammadi Begum’s Husband Refused 100,000 Rupees to Lie

If Muhammadi Begum’s husband, Mirza Sultan Muhammad, believed Hazrat Ahmad (AS) was a fraud, he had the perfect chance to expose him.

After Hazrat Ahmad (AS) passed away in 1908, Christian missionaries and Arya Samajists approached Mirza Sultan Muhammad. They wanted to use him to destroy the Ahmadiyya Movement.

They offered him a massive bribe of 100,000 rupees—which was a huge fortune at that time, equivalent to millions of dollars today—just to write a single statement claiming that Hazrat Ahmad (AS) was a liar.

What did the husband do?

He flatly refused the money and threw them out!

In 1913, Mirza Sultan Muhammad wrote a signed letter that was published for the whole world to see:

میں نے حضرت مرزا صاحب مرحوم کو ہمیشہ ایک بزرگ اور نیک انسان سمجھا ہے۔ مجھے اُن سے کوئی عداوت نہیں۔ باقی رہا مرزا احمد بیگ کی وفات کا معاملہ، سو وہ بالکل سچ ہے کہ وہ اپنی میعاد کے اندر فوت ہو گئے

“I have always regarded the late Hazrat Mirza Sahib as a noble and righteous man. I never harbored any animosity toward him. As for the death of Mirza Ahmad Baig, it is an absolute truth that he died within his appointed timeframe.”

[Letter of Mirza Sultan Muhammad, published in Chashma-e-Rahmat, 1913, p. 118]

In 1921, he gave an in-person interview repeating the exact same thing:

“The late Mirza Sahib was my elder and uncle. I never opposed him, nor did I ever say a single disrespectful word about him… As for the prophecy, its first part regarding the death of Mirza Ahmad Baig was fulfilled to the letter.”

[Interview with Mirza Sultan Muhammad, 1921; Tarikh-e-Ahmadiyyat, Vol. 2, pp. 222–223]

Even on his deathbed in 1948, he maintained this exact testimony [Al-Fazl, June 9, 1948].

Think about this logically:
– If the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum had failed, her husband would have been the first person to brag about it.
– Why would a man reject a fortune of 100,000 rupees?
– Why would he publicly confirm that his father-in-law’s death fulfilled the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum?

Because he experienced the awe of God’s sign firsthand!

Muhammadi Begum’s Entire Family Embraced Islam Ahmadiyyat

What was the final purpose of the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum?

Was it to kill people for sport? No! The Quran tells us that prophets are sent to save souls.

Remember the revelation from August 1885:

“so that they may turn back and be among those who repent.”

And that is exactly what happened!

The very family that stomped on the Quran and worshipped idols completely reformed and entered Islam Ahmadiyyat:

• Her eldest son joined Ahmadiyyat: Mirza Muhammad Ishaq Baig, the eldest son of Muhammadi Begum and Mirza Sultan Muhammad (the grandson of Ahmad Baig), accepted Ahmadiyyat in 1933. He published a public declaration in Daily Al Fazl:
“According to this prophecy, my grandfather Mirza Ahmad Baig was destroyed, and the rest of the family turned toward reformation out of fear… I swear by God, he is the very Promised Messiah foretold by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.”

[Daily Al Fazl, February 26, 1933, p. 9]

• Her other son joined Ahmadiyyat: Mirza Khurshid Baig, another son of Muhammadi Begum and Mirza Sultan Muhammad, also accepted Ahmadiyyat.

• Her grandsons became devoted Ahmadis: Her grandsons, including Mirza Majeed Baig, Mirza Aziz Baig, and Mirza Hameed Baig, all became active Ahmadi Muslims.

• Her mother joined Ahmadiyyat: Umar-un-Nisa, the mother of Muhammadi Begum (and wife of Ahmad Baig), accepted Ahmadiyyat, signed the Wasiyyat, and is buried in Bahishti Maqbarah (the heavenly graveyard).

• Her sisters and nephews joined Ahmadiyyat: Inayat Begum and Mahmuda Begum (sisters of Muhammadi Begum), as well as her brother-in-law Mirza Arshad Baig, all accepted Ahmadiyyat.

Ask yourself a simple question:

If a man made a fake prophecy about Muhammadi Begum, would her own mother, her sons, her sisters, and her cousins all accept that man as a prophet of God?

Of course not! They believed because they saw God’s sign with their own eyes.

Common Questions Answered

1. “Didn’t Hazrat Ahmad (AS) write that Muhammadi Begum would eventually marry him?”

Yes, in the original warning, it was stated that if the family continued in rebellion, Ahmad Baig would die, the husband would die within two and a half years, and Muhammadi Begum would eventually enter his marriage as a widow.

However, as Hazrat Ahmad (AS) explained, that second part only applied if the husband died!

When Ahmad Baig died in under 48 hours, the family repented in fear. Because the husband feared God and repented, God spared his life under His eternal law of mercy.

Since the husband stayed alive, how could his wife marry someone else? In Islam, a married woman cannot marry another man while her husband is alive!

In 1906, God settled the matter permanently with a final revelation:

تَكْفِيْكَ هٰذِهِ الْمَرْأَةُ

“This woman who is currently in your marriage is sufficient for you.”

[Tadhkirah, p. 596]

The marriage part was officially canceled because the family fulfilled the condition and repented.

2. “Hazrat Ahmad (AS) said his truthfulness depended on the Muhammadi Begum prophecy.”

Anti-Ahmadis love to quote lines where Hazrat Ahmad (AS) said that this prophecy would prove his truthfulness.

And it did!

The core sign was the death of Mirza Ahmad Baig within three years of Muhammadi Begum’s wedding. Ahmad Baig was the ringleader who demanded the sign, laughed at Islam, and stomped on the Quran. He died in less than six months!

Even his fiercest opponent, Maulvi Muhammad Hussain Batalwi, admitted the death happened right on time. Even the husband admitted it. Even Muhammadi Begum’s own family admitted it.

That is undeniable proof of truthfulness.

3. “Why do anti-Ahmadis make cheap attacks about Muhammadi Begum?”

Because they are copying the exact same cheap attacks that disbelievers and Christian critics made against Prophet Muhammad ﷺ!

When God commanded Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to marry Hazrat Zainab bint Jahsh (RA) in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:38) to break a pagan custom about adopted sons, pagan Arabs and hypocrites made cheap jokes and accused him of womanizing. Christian critics still use those same dirty attacks against Prophet Muhammad ﷺ today.

Anti-Ahmadis are copying the exact same disbelievers’ playbook.

They ignore the relatives stomping on the Holy Quran. They ignore them demanding a sign from God. They ignore the father dropping dead in under six months. And they reduce the serious divine prophecy of Muhammadi Begum down to cheap gossip.

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) was in his fifties, sick, and spent his nights crying in prayer for Islam. He had zero personal interest in this:

“I had no personal desire or need for this marriage. It was purely an order from God Almighty to establish a sign for those who were denying Islam.”

[A’ina-e-Kamalat-e-Islam, Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 5, p. 572]

Frequently Asked Questions

What was the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum?

It was a divine warning given to Mirza Ahmad Baig of Hoshiarpur regarding his daughter, Muhammadi Begum. He and his relatives had left Islam, mocked Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and demanded a heavenly sign. God revealed that if he married his daughter Muhammadi Begum elsewhere in defiance of God, he would die within three years of that wedding day.

When did Mirza Ahmad Baig die after marrying Muhammadi Begum away?

He died on September 30, 1892, just 5 months and 23 days after marrying Muhammadi Begum away. He died within 48 hours of developing a sudden typhoid fever, fulfilling the prophecy right on time.

Why didn’t Muhammadi Begum’s husband, Mirza Sultan Muhammad, die?

In Islam, warnings of punishment are conditional upon repentance. When Ahmad Baig died, the family was gripped by intense fear of God, offered prayers, fasted, and repented. Muhammadi Begum’s husband humbled himself and showed respect. Therefore, God spared him, exactly as God spared the people of Prophet Jonah (Yunus AS) when they repented.

What did Muhammadi Begum’s husband say about the prophecy?

Mirza Sultan Muhammad publicly testified that Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) was a righteous man and that Ahmad Baig’s death was an undeniable fulfillment of the prophecy of Muhammadi Begum. He even turned down a bribe of 100,000 rupees offered by opponents to speak against Hazrat Ahmad (AS).

Did Muhammadi Begum’s family accept Islam Ahmadiyyat?

Yes. Muhammadi Begum’s eldest son, Mirza Muhammad Ishaq Baig, accepted Ahmadiyyat in 1933. Her other son, Mirza Khurshid Baig, and her grandsons all joined Islam Ahmadiyyat. Even her mother, Umar-un-Nisa (Ahmad Baig’s widow), accepted Ahmadiyyat and is buried in Bahishti Maqbarah.

Introduction

Christian apologists often attack Islam by claiming that capital punishment for apostasy proves a religion is immoral, barbaric, or a dangerous cult.

This entire argument backfires completely.

In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is God. He is the eternal Lord who revealed the Old Testament to Moses. It was Jesus Himself who affirmed the Law of the Old Testament & commanded the stoning and execution of apostates for 1,500 years. If executing apostates is inherently immoral and evil, then Christians are condemning their own God. Meanwhile, the Holy Quran contains zero verses commanding the killing of apostates.

The Fatal Dilemma for Christian Apologists

Before examining the Biblical verses, every reader must understand the theological checkmate facing Christian critics:

• Jesus is Yahweh: In orthodox Christian doctrine, Jesus is not a secondary prophet who appeared 2,000 years ago. He is co-eternal God. Through Him all things were made (John 1:1–3).

• Jesus Revealed the Law: The God who spoke from the burning bush and delivered the laws on Mount Sinai was Jesus Christ.

• The Logical Trap: When Christian apologists call the death penalty for apostasy “immoral,” “cruel,” or “cult-like,” they are calling their own God—Jesus Christ—immoral, cruel, and cult-like.

Christians cannot dismiss this by claiming: “That was just the Old Testament, and Jesus replaced it.” God’s moral nature never changes. If executing someone for leaving their faith is fundamentally evil, an all-good God could never have commanded it in the first place.

Yet the Bible proves that God commanded exactly that.

1. Explicit Statutory Laws: God’s Codified Capital Penalties

These passages are not historical stories or actions of flawed men. They are permanent, statutory legal codes dictated directly by God in the Torah – the Old Testament.

1. Deuteronomy 13:6–10: Stoning Apostate Family Members

Biblical law does not treat apostasy as political treason against a king. It enters the home and commands believers to stone their own family members to death without showing any mercy:

“If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your friend who is as your own soul entices you secretly, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods’… you shall not yield to him or listen to him, nor shall your eye pity him, nor shall you spare him, nor shall you conceal him. But you shall kill him. Your hand shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. You shall stone him to death with stones, because he sought to draw you away from the Lord your God…”

[Deuteronomy 13:6–10]

Under Christian theology, Jesus Christ commanded a husband to throw the first stone at his apostate wife, and a father to stone his own daughter to death without pity.

2. Deuteronomy 13:12–16: The Total Annihilation of Apostate Cities

If a town decides to follow another religion, the Bible mandates total collective slaughter. Every citizen, infant, and animal must be put to the sword, and the entire city burned to ash:

“…you shall inquire and make search and ask diligently. And behold, if it be true and certain that such an abomination has been done among you, you shall surely put the inhabitants of that city to the sword, devoting it to destruction, all who are in it and its cattle, with the edge of the sword. You shall gather all its spoil into the midst of its open square and burn the city and all its spoil with fire as a whole burnt offering to the Lord your God. It shall be a heap forever. It shall not be built again.”

[Deuteronomy 13:12–16]

This was not a war against foreign enemies. It was a statutory law commanding the extermination of domestic citizens and their livestock for changing their religion.

3. Deuteronomy 17:2–7: Stoning Individual Religious Dissenters

The Bible provides formal courtroom procedures for executing any individual man or woman who practices another faith:

“If there is found among you… a man or woman who does what is evil in the sight of the Lord your God… and has gone and served other gods and worshiped them… then you shall bring out to your gates that man or woman who has done this evil thing, and you shall stone that man or woman to death with stones. On the evidence of two witnesses or of three witnesses the one who is to die shall be put to death… The hand of the witnesses shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.”

[Deuteronomy 17:2–7]

4. Leviticus 24:14–16, 23: Direct Divine Decree to Stone Blasphemers

God spoke directly to Moses in the first person, codifying death by stoning for anyone who curses or blasphemes His name:

“The Lord spoke to Moses, saying… ‘Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin. Whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him. The sojourner as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.’ … Thus the people of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses.”

[Leviticus 24:14–16, 23]

5. Deuteronomy 13:1–5 & 18:20: Executing Religious Preachers and Miracle-Workers

The Bible commands that even if a preacher performs genuine miracles, if their doctrine leads people away from the Torah, they must be executed immediately:

“If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder, and the sign or wonder that he tells you comes to pass, and if he says, ‘Let us go after other gods’… that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has taught rebellion against the Lord your God… So you shall purge the evil from your midst.”

[Deuteronomy 13:1–5]

Deuteronomy 18:20 repeats this capital mandate:

“But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that same prophet shall die.”

[Deuteronomy 18:20]

6. Exodus 22:20 & Leviticus 20:2, 27: Capital Punishment for Non-Yahwist Worship

The core covenant code delivered at Mount Sinai explicitly mandates death for anyone offering sacrifices to any other god:

• Exodus 22:20: “Whoever sacrifices to any god, other than the Lord alone, shall be devoted to destruction.” [Exodus 22:20]

• Leviticus 20:2: “Any one of the people of Israel or of the strangers who sojourn in Israel who gives any of his children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.” [Leviticus 20:2]

• Leviticus 20:27: “A man or a woman who is a medium or a necromancer shall surely be put to death. They shall be stoned with stones.” [Leviticus 20:27]

7. Zechariah 13:2–3: Parents Piercing Through Their Own Child

The Bible commands parents to kill their own son if he speaks false prophecy:

“…And if anyone again prophesies, his father and his mother who bore him will say to him, ‘You shall not live, for you speak lies in the name of the Lord.’ And his father and his mother who bore him shall pierce him through when he prophesies.“

[Zechariah 13:2–3]

Jewish Scholars Confirm

Rabbi Moses Maimonides confirms this in Guide to the Perplexed, stating that those who reject the Torah out of negligence and contempt must be put to death for blasphemy, just like the people of the lost city.

“Such an act appears to be a violation and defiance of the Law. If a person from Israel were to eat meat with milk in my presence, or wear mixed fabrics (shatnez), or shave the edges of his head out of negligence and contempt—indicating that he does not believe in the truth of this legislation—this would be considered by me as blasphemy/contempt against the Lord. He would be executed as a heretic (infidel), not under standard retaliation laws (qisas), just like the people of the Wayward City (Ir HaNidachat) who are killed out of heresy rather than retaliation. Therefore, their property is burned and not passed down to their heirs[…]”

[The Guide for the Perplexed, p.644]

The Church Encyclopedia states that Jewish law mandates execution for violators based on two or three witnesses, with no mercy—echoing Hebrews 10:28: “Whoever breaks the law of Moses must die without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.”

“28 Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

[…]

Q28: Indeed, the Law in which the Jews believe dictates the execution of anyone who violates it, if the sin is proven against him by the testimony of two or three witnesses. No pity or excuse is of any avail, and this is to declare the Law out of fear of God and respect for the commandment (Matthew 18:16).”

[The Church Encyclopedia for the New Testament Commentary, p.76]

2. Direct Divine Verdicts: God Sentencing People to Death in Real Time

Christian apologists often claim these statutes were theoretical and never actually enforced by God. Scriptural history completely disproves this claim. In multiple incidents, God personally issued real-time death warrants.

1. Numbers 15:32–36: God Personally Orders Stoning for Gathering Sticks on the Sabbath

An Israelite man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath. The people placed him in custody because the punishment was not yet clear. They asked God directly for a ruling:

“And the Lord said to Moses, ‘The man shall be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.’ And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him to death with stones, as the Lord commanded Moses.“

[Numbers 15:32–36]

This was not a human decision. Yahweh Himself handed down the capital sentence: execution by stoning for picking up dry sticks on Saturday.

2. Numbers 25:1–9: God Personally Demands Public Hanging in the Sun

When Israelites turned to the worship of Baal of Peor, God ordered the immediate execution of community leaders:

“And the Lord said to Moses, ‘Take all the chiefs of the people and hang them in the sun before the Lord, that the fierce anger of the Lord may turn away from Israel.’ And Moses said to the judges of Israel, ‘Each of you kill those of his men who have yoked themselves to Baal of Peor.'”

[Numbers 25:4–5]

When Phinehas took a spear and impaled an apostate man and a Midianite woman through their bodies, God praised him and rewarded his lineage with a perpetual covenant of peace (Numbers 25:11–13).

3. Historical Accounts of Mass Slaughters in the Bible

The Old Testament records widespread executions of religious competitors and apostates carried out under divine mandates:

• Exodus 32:25–28 (The Golden Calf Purge): Moses commanded the Levites: “Put your sword on your side each of you… and each of you kill his brother and his companion and his neighbor… And that day about three thousand men of the people fell.” [Exodus 32:25–28]

• 1 Kings 18:40 (Elijah Slaughtering 450 Prophets of Baal): After the contest on Mount Carmel, Elijah ordered: “Seize the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape… And Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon and slaughtered them there.” [1 Kings 18:40] [Arabic Scan]

• 2 Kings 10:18–28 (Jehu’s Slaughter of Baal Worshippers): King Jehu gathered all worshippers of Baal into a temple under false pretenses. Once trapped inside, he ordered his guards: “Go in and strike them down; let not a man escape. So when they put them to the sword… they demolished the house of Baal, and made it a latrine to this day.” [2 Kings 10:18–28]

• 2 Chronicles 15:12–13 (National Law Executing Non-Seekers): Under King Asa, Israel entered a binding covenant: “…that whoever would not seek the Lord, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.” [2 Chronicles 15:12–13]

• 2 Kings 23:20 (Josiah Slaughtering Priests on Altars): King Josiah executed all rival priests: “And he slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there, on the altars, and burned human bones on them.” [2 Kings 23:20]

4. The New Testament and Christian Church History

The New Testament does not condemn these Old Testament punishments as cruel or unjust. In fact, it affirms that breaking the Mosaic law resulted in merciless physical death:

“Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without mercy on the evidence of two or three witnesses. How much worse punishment, do you think, will be deserved by the one who has trampled underfoot the Son of God…”

[Hebrews 10:28–29]

The author of Hebrews uses the merciless physical execution of apostates under Moses as an unquestioned moral baseline, arguing that apostates from Christ face an even more severe eternal punishment.

Jesus Upholds the Law

Jesus never condemned the death penalty for apostasy. In Matthew 5:17–19, Jesus stated:

“Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.”

[Matthew 5:17]

In the Parable of the Ten Minas, Jesus depicted the king’s royal decree over dissenters:

“But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me.”

[Luke 19:27]

Centuries of Christian Theocratic Executions

For over a thousand years, Christian church authorities cited Deuteronomy 13 and Leviticus 24 as divine mandates to execute religious dissidents:

• The Roman Empire & Middle Ages: Byzantine legal codes, medieval Inquisitions, and the Crusades legally mandated death for heretics and apostates.

• The Protestant Reformation: John Calvin had theologian Michael Servetus burned at the stake in Geneva in 1553 specifically by citing Deuteronomy 13.

• Colonial America: Puritans in Massachusetts hanged Quakers and religious dissenters under the authority of Biblical penal law.

5. The Striking Contrast with the Holy Quran

When critics attack Islam on apostasy, they ignore a glaring theological double standard.

The Holy Quran mentions apostasy in over ten distinct verses (including Quran 2:218, 3:87–92, 3:145, 4:138, 5:55, and 16:107). In zero of these verses does God prescribe death or any worldly capital punishment.

Instead, the Holy Quran lays down a universal principle of complete freedom of conscience:

لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ

“There should be no compulsion in religion. Surely, right has become distinct from wrong.”

[Quran 2:256]

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never executed anyone merely for changing their religion. When a Bedouin revoked his pledge of Islam three times in Medina, the Prophet ﷺ let him leave unharmed (Sahih al-Bukhari 7322). For an in-depth analysis, read our complete guide on What Is the Punishment for Apostasy in Islam? The Truth from the Quran and our refutation of the wartime treason narration in Hadith: “Whoever Changes His Religion, Kill Him” Explained.

Introduction

Many critics quote a single Hadith to claim that Islam executes anyone who leaves the faith:

مَنْ بَدَّلَ دِينَهُ فَاقْتُلُوهُ

“Whoever changes his religion, kill him.“

[Sahih al-Bukhari 6922]

This claim is completely false.

The Holy Quran contains zero verses prescribing the death penalty for apostasy, and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never executed anyone for leaving Islam.

Furthermore, if you take this statement literally without context, it creates an immediate absurdity. It does not say “whoever leaves Islam.” It says “whoever changes his religion”—which taken literally would mean executing non-Muslims who convert to Islam!

The statement was never an unconditional decree against personal faith.

Context

What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ actually mean?

Other authentic Hadiths explain this statement clearly. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abu Qilaba clarifies:

وَاللَّهِ مَا قَتَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَحَدًا قَطُّ إِلاَّ فِي إِحْدَى ثَلاَثِ خِصَالٍ رَجُلٌ قَتَلَ بِجِنَايَةِ نَفْسٍ فَقُتِلَ، أَوْ رَجُلٌ زَنَى بَعْدَ إِحْصَانٍ، أَوْ رَجُلٌ حَارَبَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَارْتَدَّ عَنِ الإِسْلاَمِ

Narrated Abu Qilaba:

“By Allah, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ never killed anyone except in one of the following three situations:

• A person who killed somebody unjustly (in Qisas).

• A married person who committed illegal sexual intercourse.

• A man who fought against Allah and His Apostle and deserted Islam and became an apostate.“

[Sahih al-Bukhari 6899]

In Sunan an-Nasa’i, Hazrat Aisha (RA) confirms:

لاَ يَحِلُّ دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ إِلاَّ فِي إِحْدَى ثَلاَثِ حُرَمٍ زَانٍ بَعْدَ إِحْصَانٍ فَعَلَيْهِ الرَّجْمُ أَوْ رَجُلٌ قَتَلَ رَجُلاً مُتَعَمِّدًا فَعَلَيْهِ الْقَتْلُ أَوْ رَجُلٌ خَرَجَ مِنَ الإِسْلاَمِ يُحَارِبُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَرَسُولَهُ يُقْتَلُ أَوْ يُصْلَبُ أَوْ يُنْفَى مِنَ الأَرْضِ

Narrated Aisha (RA):

“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘It is not permissible to shed the blood of a Muslim except in three cases: An adulterer who had been married… a man who killed another man intentionally… and a man who left Islam and waged war against Allah, the Might and Sublime, and His Messenger, who should be killed, or crucified, or banished from the land.‘”

[Sunan an-Nasa’i 4048]

These narrations clarify the entire issue.

The Hadith is not talking about private personal belief. It refers strictly to apostasy combined with rebellion and treason—leaving the community to physically wage war against the Muslims.

What Was the Example of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?

When people left Islam peacefully without committing treason, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never harmed them:

• The Bedouin in Medina: A Bedouin came to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ three times publicly demanding to revoke his pledge of Islam (“Cancel my pledge”). The Prophet ﷺ refused to release him spiritually, but let him walk out of Medina completely unharmed [Sahih al-Bukhari 7322].

• The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ formally signed a treaty agreeing that any Muslim who left Islam and returned to the Meccan pagans would not be pursued or harmed [Sahih al-Bukhari 2700].

If “Whoever changes his religion, kill him” meant killing every apostate, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would never have let apostates walk away safely.

For a full breakdown of all Quranic verses on freedom of conscience, read our master study: What Is the Punishment for Apostasy in Islam? The Truth from the Quran.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does “Whoever changes his religion, kill him” mean?

This Hadith refers strictly to wartime treason and armed rebellion against the state. Parallel authentic Hadiths in Sahih al-Bukhari 6899 and Sunan an-Nasa’i 4048 explicitly state that the death penalty applies to “a man who left Islam and waged war against Allah and His Messenger”.

Does Bukhari 6922 contradict the Quran?

When taken out of context as an order to execute peaceful apostates, it contradicts Quran 2:256 (“There is no compulsion in religion”). However, when understood in its authentic context of armed treason during war, there is zero contradiction.

Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ kill people for leaving Islam?

No. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never executed anyone solely for changing their religion. In Sahih al-Bukhari 7322, an individual revoked his pledge of Islam in Medina and the Prophet ﷺ let him walk away safely without harm.

Introduction

Many non-Muslims allege that Islam calls for the killing of those who leave this religion.

This is completely false.

The Holy Quran contains zero verses prescribing any worldly punishment or death penalty for apostasy. The example of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the exact opposite. He did not kill a single person for leaving Islam, and we have authentic historical examples where he allowed individuals to leave Islam without punishing them.

What Does the Holy Quran Say About Apostasy?

The Holy Quran mentions apostasy in numerous verses. In every single verse, Allah mentions zero worldly punishment for it.

Verse 1: Quran 2:256

The Quran lays down an absolute foundational rule:

لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ

“There should be no compulsion in religion. Surely, right has become distinct from wrong.”

[Quran 2:256]

If Islam ordered people to be killed for leaving, that would be the highest form of compulsion.

Verse 2: Quran 18:29

Allah makes faith a voluntary personal choice:

وَقُلِ الْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ فَمَن شَاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن وَمَن شَاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ

“And say, ‘It is the truth from your Lord; wherefore let him who will, believe, and let him who will, disbelieve.‘”

[Quran 18:29]

Belief and disbelief are left entirely to the individual.

Verse 3: Quran 4:137

This verse completely destroys the claim of a death penalty:

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَّمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا

“Those who believe, then disbelieve, then again believe, then disbelieve, and then increase in disbelief, Allah will never forgive them nor will He guide them to the way.”

[Quran 4:137]

Look at what Allah describes:

• A person believes.

• Then they disbelieve.

• Then they believe again.

• Then they disbelieve a second time.

• Then they increase in disbelief.

If Islam executed apostates, how could someone leave Islam, return, and leave it again?

A person killed after their first disbelief could never commit apostasy twice. This verse proves there is no death penalty in Islam for leaving the faith.

Verse 4: Quran 3:72

During the life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Medina, a group of Jews planned a scheme to create doubt:

وَقَالَت طَّائِفَةٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنزِلَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَجْهَ النَّهَارِ وَاكْفُرُوا آخِرَهُ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ

“And a section of the People of the Book say, ‘Believe in that which has been revealed unto the believers in the early part of the day, and disbelieve in the latter part thereof, that perchance they may return.'”

[Quran 3:72]

In Tafsir Ibn Kathir [Vol. 2, p. 59], Mujahid explains:

يعني يهود، صَلَّت مع النبي ﷺ صلاة الفجر وكفروا آخر النهار، مكراً منهم، ليُرُوا الناس أن قد بدت لهم منه الضلالة، بعد أن كانوا اتبعوه.

“This refers to the Jews who prayed the Fajr prayer with the Prophet ﷺ and disbelieved at the end of the day, as a plot from them, to show the people that misguidance had become apparent to them from him after they had followed him.”

[Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Vol. 2, p. 59]

They converted in the morning and left Islam at sunset. Not one of them was killed, arrested, or harmed.

If Islam prescribed death for apostasy, this plot would have been impossible to attempt.

Verse 5: Quran 88:21–22 & 10:99

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was sent only to convey the message, not to force hearts:

فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ ۝ لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ

“Admonish, therefore, for thou art but an admonisher; Thou art not appointed a warden over them.“

[Quran 88:21–22]

Allah also states:

وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَن فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعًا ۚ أَفَأَنتَ تُكْرِهُ النَّاسَ حَتَّىٰ يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ

“And if thy Lord had enforced His will, all who are on the earth would have believed together. Wilt thou, then, force men to become believers?“

[Quran 10:99]

Over 20 Additional Quranic Verses on Freedom of Religion

• “…and whoso among you turns back from his faith and dies while he is a disbeliever, their works shall be vain in this world and the next…” [Quran 2:218]

• “…and if they turn back, then thy duty is only to convey the message…” [Quran 3:21]

• “…how shall Allah guide a people who have disbelieved after having believed… except those who repent thereafter and amend…” [Quran 3:87–90]

• “O ye who believe! Whoso among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will soon bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him…” [Quran 5:55]

• “The duty of the Messenger is only to convey the message. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you hide.” [Quran 5:100]

• “Say, ‘I am not appointed a guardian over you.‘” [Quran 6:67]

• “And We have not made thee a keeper over them, nor art thou over them a guardian.” [Quran 6:108]

• “Pharaoh said, ‘Believe ye in him before I give you leave? Surely, I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and then I will crucify you all.” [Quran 7:124–125]

• “…and whoever goes astray, he goes astray only to his own loss; and I am not a keeper over you.” [Quran 10:109]

• “…thy duty is only to convey the message, and Ours is to reckon.” [Quran 13:41]

• “But if they turn away, thy duty is only the clear conveyance of the message.” [Quran 16:83]

• “…and We have not sent thee as a keeper over them.” [Quran 17:55]

• “Pharaoh said, ‘Believe ye in him before I give you leave?… Surely, I will crucify you on the trunks of palm-trees…” [Quran 20:72]

• “…and upon the Messenger lies only the clear conveyance of the Message.” [Quran 24:55]

• “Pharaoh said, ‘You have believed in him before I gave you leave?… I will surely crucify you all together.” [Quran 26:50]

• “Surely, thou canst not guide whomsoever thou lovest, but Allah guides whomsoever He pleases.” [Quran 28:57]

• “…whosoever goes astray, goes astray only to his own loss; and thou art not a keeper over them.” [Quran 39:42]

• “But if they turn away, We have not sent thee as a guardian over them. Thy duty is only to convey the Message.” [Quran 42:49]

• “Surely, those who turn their backs after guidance has become clear to them, Satan has seduced them…” [Quran 47:26]

• “We know best what they say; and thou hast not been appointed to compel them.” [Quran 50:46]

• “…but if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger lies only the clear delivery of the message.” [Quran 64:13]

• “…many among the People of the Book wish to turn you back into disbelievers after you have believed… but pardon them and pass by them until Allah brings about His command.” [Quran 2:110]

Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ Ever Execute an Apostate?

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never killed anyone for leaving Islam.

1. The Bedouin Who Cancelled His Pledge (Sahih al-Bukhari 7322)

عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، أَنَّ أَعْرَابِيًّا بَايَعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ، فَأَصَابَ الأَعْرَابِيَّ وَعْكٌ بِالْمَدِينَةِ، فَأَتَى الأَعْرَابِيُّ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي‏.‏ فَأَبَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي‏.‏ فَأَبَى، ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ فَقَالَ أَقِلْنِي بَيْعَتِي‏.‏ فَأَبَى، فَخَرَجَ الأَعْرَابِيُّ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏”‏ إِنَّمَا الْمَدِينَةُ كَالْكِيرِ، تَنْفِي خَبَثَهَا، وَيَنْصَعُ طَيِّبُهَا ‏”‏‏.‏

Narrated Jabir bin ‘Abdullah (RA):

“A Bedouin gave the Pledge of allegiance for embracing Islam to Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, and then he got an attack of fever in Medina and came to Allah’s Messenger ﷺ and said: ‘O Allah’s Messenger! Cancel my pledge.’

Allah’s Messenger ﷺ refused to do so. The Bedouin came to him again and said, ‘Cancel my pledge,’ but he refused again. And then again, the Bedouin came to him and said, ‘Cancel my pledge,’ and Allah’s Messenger ﷺ refused.

The Bedouin finally went away, and Allah’s Messenger ﷺ said: ‘Medina is like a pair of bellows (furnace), it expels its impurities while it brightens and clears its good.’“

[Sahih al-Bukhari 7322]

The Bedouin renounced his pledge of Islam three times directly before the Prophet ﷺ in Medina. The Prophet ﷺ did not execute him, jail him, or harm him. He let him walk away freely.

2. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (Sahih al-Bukhari 2700)

قَالَ صَالَحَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُشْرِكِينَ يَوْمَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ عَلَى ثَلاَثَةِ أَشْيَاءَ عَلَى أَنَّ مَنْ أَتَاهُ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ رَدَّهُ إِلَيْهِمْ، وَمَنْ أَتَاهُمْ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَمْ يَرُدُّوهُ

Narrated Al-Bara’ bin ‘Azib (RA):

“On the day of Hudaibiya, the Prophet ﷺ made a peace treaty with the Al-Mushrikun on three conditions:

• The Prophet ﷺ would return to them any person from Al-Mushrikun [who came as a Muslim].

• Al-Mushrikun pagans would not return any of the Muslims going to them [who left Islam].

• The Prophet ﷺ and his companions would come to Makkah the following year…”

[Sahih al-Bukhari 2700]

The Prophet ﷺ signed a treaty explicitly agreeing that any Muslim who apostatized and joined the pagans in Mecca would be allowed to go freely. He would never have agreed to this if apostasy required execution.

Refutation of Misquoted Hadiths

Critics and extremists ignore the Quran and Sunnah, and quote a few isolated Hadiths out of context.

1. “Whoever Changes His Religion, Kill Him”

Opponents quote this line from Ibn Abbas (RA): “Whoever changes his religion, kill him” (man baddala dīnahu faqtulūhu).

Taken literally without context, this would mean killing a Christian or Jew who converts to Islam.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ explained the exact meaning in Sahih al-Bukhari:

وَاللَّهِ مَا قَتَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَحَدًا قَطُّ إِلاَّ فِي إِحْدَى ثَلاَثِ خِصَالٍ رَجُلٌ قَتَلَ بِجِنَايَةِ نَفْسٍ فَقُتِلَ، أَوْ رَجُلٌ زَنَى بَعْدَ إِحْصَانٍ، أَوْ رَجُلٌ حَارَبَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَارْتَدَّ عَنِ الإِسْلاَمِ

Narrated Abu Qilaba:

“By Allah, Allah’s Messenger ﷺ never killed anyone except in one of the following three situations:

• A person who killed somebody unjustly (in Qisas).

• A married person who committed illegal sexual intercourse.

• A man who fought against Allah and His Apostle and deserted Islam and became an apostate.“

[Sahih al-Bukhari 6899]

In Sunan an-Nasa’i, Hazrat Aisha (RA) confirms:

لاَ يَحِلُّ دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ إِلاَّ فِي إِحْدَى ثَلاَثِ حُرَمٍ زَانٍ بَعْدَ إِحْصَانٍ فَعَلَيْهِ الرَّجْمُ أَوْ رَجُلٌ قَتَلَ رَجُلاً مُتَعَمِّدًا فَعَلَيْهِ الْقَتْلُ أَوْ رَجُلٌ خَرَجَ مِنَ الإِسْلاَمِ يُحَارِبُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَرَسُولَهُ يُقْتَلُ أَوْ يُصْلَبُ أَوْ يُنْفَى مِنَ الأَرْضِ

Narrated Aisha (RA):

“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘It is not permissible to shed the blood of a Muslim except in three cases: An adulterer who had been married… a man who killed another man intentionally… and a man who left Islam and waged war against Allah, the Might and Sublime, and His Messenger, who should be killed, or crucified, or banished from the land.‘”

[Sunan an-Nasa’i 4048]

The Hadith is not talking about personal belief. It refers strictly to apostasy plus treason and rebellion—leaving the community to physically fight against the Muslims.

2. Mu’adh bin Jabal in Yemen (Sahih al-Bukhari 6923)

Critics cite the narration where Mu’adh bin Jabal (RA) told Abu Musa al-Ash’ari (RA) to execute an apostate in Yemen.

However, in Al-Musannaf of Imam Abdur-Razzaq as-San’ani [Vol. 10, p. 466], the full narration shows that Mu’adh was quoting that exact same Hadith:

أبي بردة قال : قدم على أبي موسى الأشعري معاذ بن جبل باليمن ، فإذا برجل عنده ، فقال : ما هذا ؟ فقال : رجل كان يهودياً فأسلم ثم تهود ، ونحن نريده على الإسلام منذ – أحسبه قال – شهرين ، فقال معاذ : والله لا أقعد حتى تضربوا عنقه ، ثم قال معاذ : قضى الله ورسوله أن من رجع عن دينه فاقتلوه ، أو قال : من بدّل دينه فاقتلوه

Narrated Abu Burdah:

“Mu’adh said: ‘By Allah, I will not sit down until you strike his neck.’ Then Mu’adh said: ‘Allah and His Messenger decreed that whoever turns back from his religion, kill him; or he said: whoever changes his religion, kill him.’“

[Al-Musannaf of Abdur-Razzaq, Vol. 10, p. 466, Hadith 18972]

Mu’adh was quoting the exact same narration of Ibn Abbas (RA) that applies to apostasy combined with rebellion and treason.

This is a single incident with no details about the individual’s crimes. An isolated report cannot create a general rule that contradicts the Quran and the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

3. Ali (RA) and the Burning Incident (Sahih al-Bukhari 6922)

Opponents also bring up the narration where people called Zanadiqa were burnt by Ali (RA):

عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، أَنَّ عَلِيًّا ـ رضى الله عنه ـ حَرَّقَ قَوْمًا، فَبَلَغَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ فَقَالَ لَوْ كُنْتُ أَنَا لَمْ أُحَرِّقْهُمْ لِأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لاَ تُعَذِّبُوا بِعَذَابِ اللَّهِ‏.‏ وَلَقَتَلْتُهُمْ لِقَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏”‏ مَنْ بَدَّلَ دِينَهُ فَاقْتُلُوهُ ‏”‏‏.‏

Narrated Ikrima:

“Ali burnt some people. The news reached Ibn Abbas, who said: ‘If I had been in his place, I would not have burnt them, for the Prophet ﷺ said: Do not punish with Allah’s punishment (fire). I would have killed them according to the statement of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ: Whoever changes his religion, kill him.‘”

[Sahih al-Bukhari 6922]

This narration is vague and gives zero details about what crimes these individuals committed.

A single, isolated incident of a companion cannot be taken as a general rule, especially when key details are missing. The Holy Quran and the authentic Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ come first.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Holy Quran punish apostasy?

No. There is zero punishment for leaving Islam in the Holy Quran. The Quran mentions apostasy in dozens of verses and describes it strictly as a spiritual matter judged by Allah in the Hereafter (e.g. Quran 4:137, 2:217).

Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ever kill anyone for leaving Islam?

No. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never executed anyone simply for changing their religion. In Sahih al-Bukhari 7322, a Bedouin took back his pledge of Islam three times and the Prophet ﷺ let him walk out of Medina safely. In the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (Sahih al-Bukhari 2700), he agreed that apostates were free to leave.

What is the meaning of “Whoever changes his religion, kill him”?

This statement was made about wartime treason. Parallel authentic Hadiths in Sahih al-Bukhari 6899 and Sunan an-Nasa’i 4048 state that the death penalty applies only to a person who left Islam and took up arms to wage war against the community.

Why do some people believe Islam kills apostates?

In early history, leaving Islam almost always meant joining enemy tribes to wage war against Muslims. Some scholars confused political treason during war with a peaceful change of belief.

Introduction

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) details the continuous reality of divine revelation, the diverse categories of spiritual converse with God, and how living communion with the Creator remains open through Islam.

Author: Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian (AS)

Compiler: Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad, Khalifatul Masih IV (RH)

Section: Divine Discourse & Signs

Excerpt 56

When God Almighty intends to inform His servant of a matter pertaining to the realm of the Unknown, whether He does it in response to His servant’s prayer or on His own, He brings down upon him a sort of unconsciousness and all of a sudden he loses touch with his surroundings. In that state, he completely loses awareness of even his own existence.

Like a diver who plunges down to the bottom of a pool, he is completely submerged and drowned in that state of selflessness, unawareness and unconsciousness. When, in the end, he breaks surface like a diver with whom he shares his experience to a large degree and is delivered from that state of unawareness, he becomes conscious of a resonance within him.

As that resonance fades out, he becomes aware of the presence of a most pleasant, well balanced and exquisite communication within him. And this experience is so strange and sublime that it is beyond one’s power to describe it in words. It is this experience which reveals to one the existence of a flowing river of inner wisdom. It is through this experience of near unconsciousness that a servant of God receives from God, answers to all his supplications in an extremely exquisite and pleasant tone.

Then, in response to whatever question takes shape in that state of semi unconsciousness, God reveals to him such profound knowledge as is impossible for a man to discover otherwise. This in itself results in his gaining greater faith in God and a better understanding of His wondrous ways. Man’s supplication and God’s response to it by way of manifestation of His being the true object of worship is an experience which enables man to behold God, as if he were seeing Him in this very world; thus be begins to belong to both worlds simultaneously.

[Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 1, footnote pp. 260 -262]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 70]

Excerpt 57

In another type of revelation which has nothing to do with the subjective experience of the heart, one hears a voice from without as if someone were speaking from behind a curtain. This voice is very pleasing and cheerful and flows at a somewhat brisk pace fillings one’s heart with ecstasy. A man’s mind may have been occupied in deep thought when all of a sudden this voice is heard.

Having heard this voice he is left wondering where it came from and who it was who addressed him. He looks to and fro like a surprised person and then he begins to realize that the voice had proceeded from an angel. This external voice is often heard and carries a glad tiding at a time when someone has been excessively worried and laden with grief concerning some problem.

[Braheen-e-Ahmadiyya: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 1, footnote p. 287]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 73]

Excerpt 58

It is so decreed that one who has a measure of light will be further enlightened. And the one who has nothing is given nothing. And one who is enlightened with the faculty of sight is the one who benefits from the light of the sun. Likewise the one who does not possess the light of eyesight remains incapable of seeing the light of the sun.

Verily, a person who is less enlightened within, is also less enlightened from without. The one who is provided more abundantly with internal light will also benefit more abundantly from external light.

[Braheen-e-Ahmadiyya: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 1, footnote pp. 195-196]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 72]

Excerpt 59

God Almighty has divided His wonderful universe into three categories. First, the world which is manifest and can be conceived through the eyes and the ears and other sensory organs, directly or indirectly with the help of Secondly, the world which is hidden and which can be understood through deductive reasoning and hypothesizing. Thirdly, the world which lies even farther than the hidden world, so hard to conceive and almost beyond the reach of imagination.

Very few are those who are aware of its existence. That is an entirely obscure world which cannot be conceived through deduction but is only imagined. One can have access to it only with the help of spiritual vision or revelation or a word from God and not by any other means. As is evident from the unchanging Will of God, manifested in nature, one can safely deduce that as God has provided man with the apparatus to understand the first two categories of His creation mentioned above, similarly He must have provided man with the apparatus and instruments to conceive that world of His creation which is mentioned under the third category.

And that apparatus (as we have already mentioned) comprises spiritual vision, revelation and the word of God. This mode of communication can never be conceived to be inoperative or to have ceased altogether in any age. Nay, but those who fulfilled the pre requisite have always been gifted with this and will continue to be gifted with the same.

[Surma Chashm-e-Arya: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 2, p. 127-128]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 73]

Introduction

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) sets forth the unambiguous tenets of faith adhered to by the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community, rooted entirely in the Holy Quran, the Sunnah, and pure Islamic monotheism (Tawhid).

Excerpt 50

Gist of our faith is: La Ilaha Illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah. (There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.) Our belief, which we hold in this life here on earth and to which we will continue to adhere firmly till the time that we pass on to the next world, is that our spiritual leader and master, Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be on him, is the Seal of the Prophets and the Best of the Messengers.

At his hands religion has been perfected and blessing of Allah has been consummated which lead man to the right path and further on to God Himself. We hold this positive belief with absolute certainty that the Holy Quran is the seal of all Divine books and not an iota can be added to or subtracted from its prescribed teachings, inhibitions, commands and injunctions.

There will be no revelation or word from God which may amend or abrogate or change or alter any of the injunctions of the Holy Quran. If anyone subscribes to such views, in our opinion, he ceases to belong to the body of believers and becomes an infidel thereby.

[Izala-e-Auham: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 3:, p. 170]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 62]

Excerpt 51

We do believe that there is none worthy of worship except GodAlmighty and Sayyedena Hadhrat Muhammad, the Chosen One, may peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is His Messenger and the Khatamul Anbiya. We believe that angels are a reality, that Resurrection is a reality and the Day of Judgement is areality; that Heaven is reality and so is Hell.We do believe that whatever the Glorious and Majestic God has stated in the Holy Quran and whatever our Prophet, may peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has stated is all, according to the aforementioned statement, the truth.

We do believe that the person who subtracts an iota from the Islamic law or adds to it as much, or lays the foundation in any manner for rejection of Islamic injunctions, or attempts to declare unlawful what has been made lawful in Islam, is an infidel and a renegade to Islam. We admonish our Jamaat that they must adhere tenaciously to the fundamental article of Islamic faith. “There is no God but Allah, Muhammad is His Messenger” as long as they live and that they should die holding fast to the same belief.

Also they must have firm faith in all the Messengers of Allah and revealed Books which have been authenticated by the Holy Quran. They should abide strictly by the Quranic injunctions. They should strictly observe Prayers and Fast, pay Zakat and perform the Haj (pilgrimage). They should observe Islam by fully complying with all the injunctions, obligations and prohibitions pronounced by God and His Messenger.

In short, all such matters, be they beliefs or deeds, on which there was consensus of opinion among our righteous predecessors and as are understood to be Islam by the general consensus of opinion of those who follow the traditions of the Holy Prophet of Islam, may peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, should be complied with as being obligatory.

We call to witness the Heaven and the Earth, that exactly is our Faith.”

[Ayyam-us-Sulh, 1st Edition: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 14, p 323]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 64]

Excerpt 52

ye who inhabit the earth! And ye human spirits who dwell in the East or in the West! I invite you most earnestly to accept the fact that the only true faith today in the. world is Islam and that the True God is that God who has been mentioned in the Holy Quran, and that Prophet who possesses eternal spiritual life the one who sits on the throne of glory and purity is the Holy Prophet Muhammad, the chosen one, may peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

[Tiryaq-ul-Qulub: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 15, p. 141]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 64]

In this triumphant concluding discourse, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) affirms the ultimate victory of truth and the universal ascendancy of Islamic monotheism over all opposing forces.

Author: Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian (AS)

Compiler: Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad, Khalifatul Masih IV (RH)

Section: Triumph of Islam

Excerpt 77

People of the world may be inclined to think that it is Christianity which may ultimately spread throughout the world, or it may be Buddhism which will prevail in the end. But they are certainly wrong in these conjectures. Remember that nothing happens on this Earth unless it has been so willed in Heaven. And, it is the God of Heaven who revealed to me that ultimately it will be the religion of Islam which will conquer the hearts of people.

[Barahin-e-Ahmadiyya, Pt. 5: Ruhani Khaza’in Vol. 21, p 427]
[Selected Writings of the Promised Messiah, p. 99]
